chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 3. Objectives of the Law The objectives of this Law are to: (a) create a Plateau St
chunks.text: 3. Objectives of the Law The objectives of this Law are to: (a) create a Plateau State Electricity Market that is commercially-sound, technically-compliant, well - funded and financially-viable; (b) facilitate investments and innovation in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (c) establish a regulatory framework and licensing regime for the conduct of electricity operations by entities operating in the Plateau State Electricity Market and for the delivery of services by such entities to electricity consumers located in the State; (d) ensure the safe, reliable and efficient interconnection of the Plateau State Electricity Market with the national electricity market; (e) facilitate the delivery of affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern public electricity access to electricity consumers in the State; (f) promote the adoption of diverse , secure and environmentally-sustainable energy sources, energy efficiency and demand side management in the State; (g) facilitate the adoption of clean and modern technology for the delivery of electricity access to electricity consumers in the State; 11 (h) foster competition in the Plateau State Electricity Market, and protect the interests and welfare of electricity consumers in the State; (i) incentivise the behaviour of the Commission, licensees, electricity consumers, investors and other market participants in the Plateau Electricity Market with the aim of ensuring the delivery of constant, reliable and cost-efficient electricity supply to electricity consumers in the State; (j) establish a mechanism for electricity planning in the State; (k) promote the provision of off -grid solutions for households, and micro, small and medium scale enterprises in the State; (l) promote the electrification of unserved and under-served areas of the State; and (m) contribute to the sustainable development of the State. PART II ADMINISTRATION OF THE PLATEAU STATE ELECTRICITY MARKET

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 4. The Role of the Plateau State Government The role of the Plateau State Governmen
chunks.text: 4. The Role of the Plateau State Government The role of the Plateau State Government shall be to: (a) facilitate and support the development of a sustainable electricity sector in the State; (b) promote an enabling environment for investments in and the development of the electricity sector in the State; (c) collaborate with the Federal Government to facilitate the establishment and operation of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (d) provide a platform that enables the continuing growth and viability of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (e) promote the development and use of renewable energy sources for generation of electricity in the State, including collaborating with the Federal Government on the same; (f) ensure the security of electricity infrastructure in the State; and (g) ensure and protect the independence of the Commission.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 5. The Role of the Ministry of Water Resources and Energy The role of the Ministry
chunks.text: 5. The Role of the Ministry of Water Resources and Energy The role of the Ministry shall be to: (a) oversee the coordinated planning, policy-making, evolution, administration and monitoring of the electricity sector in the State; (b) promote the development and utilization of renewable energy sources in the State; 12 (c) represent the State in all matters pertaining to electricity in the State; (d) supervise, monitor and evaluate the activities of the Agency; (e) collaborate with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government and the State to facilitate the establishment and operation of the Plateau Electricity Market; (f) promote, facilitate and support research and development in the electricity sector; (g) report developments in the electricity sector to the State Executive Council; and (h) perform any other function as may be assigned to it by the Governor.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 6. Policy Directives to the Commission (1) The Honourable Commissioner may give gen
chunks.text: 6. Policy Directives to the Commission (1) The Honourable Commissioner may give general policy directi ves to the Commission on matters concerning the electricity sector in the State in line with the provisions of this Law and the Commission shall take the directives into consideration in discharging its functions, provided that such directives are not in conflict with this Law. (2) All general policy directives issued pursuant to this section shall be published on the website of the Commission. (3) In the execution of the role of the Ministry and relationship with the Commission, the Honourable Commissioner shall at all times take steps to protect the Commission from interference and ensure that the autonomy of the Commission, in regard to the discharge of its functions and operations and exercise of its powers under this Law, is protected and not compromised in any manner whatsoever. Part III ESTABLISHMENT OF THE PLATEAU STATE ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 7. Establishment of the Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission (1) There i
chunks.text: 7. Establishment of the Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission (1) There is established the Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission (referred to in this Law as “the Commission”). (2) The Commission shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal and shall, in its corporate name, be capable of: (a) suing and being sued; (b) acquiring, owning, holding, mortgaging, developing, disposing and otherwise dealing howsoever with property, whether movable or immovable; (c) entering into contracts and incurring obligations; and (d) doing or performing all other things or acts in furtherance of the provisions of this Law which may be lawfully done or performed by a body corporate. 13 (3) Except as otherwise provided in this Law, the Commission shall be autonomous in the performance of and in carrying out its functions and duties and in the exercise of its powers. (4) The day-to-day business of the Commission shall be performed through such departments as the Commission may consider necessary for the effective and efficient discharge of its functions under this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 8. Composition of the Commission (1) The Commission shall co nsist of five (5) Comm
chunks.text: 8. Composition of the Commission (1) The Commission shall co nsist of five (5) Commissioners, who shall be responsible for the management and general administration of the Commission. (2) The five (5) Commissioners shall comprise: (a) two (2) Non-Executive Commissioners appointed from outside the public sector , one of whom shall be appointed as the Chairperson; and (b) three (3) Executive Commissioners, one of whom shall be appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of the Commission. (3) The Commission shall however not be incapacitated from carrying out its functions and exercising its powers by virtue of any vacancy in the composition of the Commission or defect in the appointment of any Commissioner. 9. Functions of the Commissioners The Commissioners shall: (a) be solely responsible for taking administrative decisions in regard to the internal affairs of the Commission and for taking regulatory decisions in regard to the operations of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (b) exercise the functions and powers of the Commission; (c) review and approve the operating, business and strategic plans of the Commission; (d) determine the terms and conditions of service of staff of the Commission; (e) structure the Commission into such number of departments as it deems fit for the effective discharge of the functions of the Commission; and (f) carry out such other functions as may be necessary for the efficient and effective administration of the Commission under this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 10. Appointment of Non-Executive Commissioners (1) The Non-Executive Commissioners s
chunks.text: 10. Appointment of Non-Executive Commissioners (1) The Non-Executive Commissioners shall be appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Honourable Commissioner and each appointment shall be confirmed by the House. 14 (2) A person shall be qualified for appointment as a Non-Executive Commissioner if such person: (a) is a holder of a university degree recognized in Nigeria in the fields of law, accountancy, economics, finance, administration, consumer affairs, energy, engineering or regulatory affairs; (b) has not less than fifteen (15) years working experience in the relevant field, seven (7) of which are at a senior management level; and (c) is a highly respected person of reputable character. (3) The Non-Executive Commissioners shall hold office on a part-time basis for a period of four (4) years, provided that, to ensure continuity in the Commission, the first Chairperson shall be appointed for a period of five (5) years. (4) The Non-Executive Commissioners shall be eligible for reappointment for one (1) further term of four (4) years only.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 11. Appointment of Executive Commissioners (1) The Executive Commissioners shall be
chunks.text: 11. Appointment of Executive Commissioners (1) The Executive Commissioners shall be appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Honourable Commissioner following a competitive recruitment process to be conducted by the Ministry and each appointment shall be confirmed by the House. (2) A person shall be qualified for appointment as an Executive Commissioner if such person: (a) is a holder of a university degree recognized in Nigeria in the fields of law, accountancy , economics, finance, administration, consumer affairs, energy or engineering or regulatory affairs; (b) has not less than fifteen (15) years working experience in the relevant field, seven (7) of which are at a senior management level; (c) is a highly respected person of reputable character; and (d) has extensive managerial, technical or professional knowledge of and experience in infrastructure service operations and management and/or regulation. (3) The Executive Commissioners shall be appointed for an initial term of four (4) years and shall be eligible, subject to satisfactory performance , for reappointment for one (1) further term of four (4) years only. (4) Except as provided in this Law, t he terms and conditions of appointment of the Executive Commissioners shall be specified in their respective letters of appointment.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 12. General Rules Applicable to the Appointment of Commissioners (1) A person shall
chunks.text: 12. General Rules Applicable to the Appointment of Commissioners (1) A person shall not be appointed as a Commissioner who: 15 (a) is not a citizen of Nigeria; (b) has, under the laws in force in any country: (i) been certified to be of unsound mind; (ii) been adjudged or declared bankrupt and has not been discharged; (iii) made an assignment to or arrangement or composition with his creditors, which has not been rescinded or set aside; (iv) been convicted of any criminal offence by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction except for traffic offences; or (v) at any time been removed from an office of trust on account of misconduct; (c) has been disqualified or suspended from practicing his /her profession by the order of a competent authority; or (d) has a financial interest in any business connected, directly or indirectly, with the Plateau State Electricity Market or the national electricity market , or is engaged in any activity for remuneration or otherwise connected with the Plateau State Electricity Market or national electricity market, or is a relative of a person who has such an interest or is engaged in such an activity, unless the financial interest is terminated prior to the appointment taking effect. (2) In appointing Commissioners, the Governor shall take into account the need to have in the Commission the appropriate mix of knowledge, skills, experience, and attributes such as age, culture and gender.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 13. Resignation from the Commission A Commissioner may resign from his/her office by
chunks.text: 13. Resignation from the Commission A Commissioner may resign from his/her office by giving not less than three (3) months written notice to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner. 14. Suspension or Removal of Commissioner (1) A Commissioner may be suspended or removed from office by the Governor , on the recommendation of the Honourable Commissioner, if he/she: (a) is found to be unqualified for appointment as a Commissioner pursuant to the provisions of this Law or has become unqualified subsequent to his/her appointment; (b) is in breach of the terms and conditions of his/her appointment; (c) has demonstrated such inability to effectively carry out the functions of his/her office; 16 (d) is guilty of gross misconduct in relation to his/her duties and performance of his/her functions as a Commissioner, which gross misconduct has been established by an investigative panel established by the Commission; (e) is in breach of the Commission’s Code of Ethics; (f) becomes mentally or physically incapable of efficiently carrying out his/her functions as a Commissioner; or (g) has been absent from five (5) consecutive meetings of the Commission without the consent of the Chair person, and in the case of the Chair person, without the consent of the Honourable Commissioner, except where good reason is shown for such absence. (2) A Commissioner shall not be removed unless the request is made by the Governor and supported by a simple majority vote of the House.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 15. Vacancies in the Commission (1) A vacancy in the Commission shall occur, where a
chunks.text: 15. Vacancies in the Commission (1) A vacancy in the Commission shall occur, where a Commissioner: (a) dies; (b) is removed from office in accordance with this Law; (c) resigns from office; or (d) completes his/her tenure of office. (2) A vacancy in the Commission shall be filled in accordance with the requirements of this Law. (3) Where a vacancy in the Commission is created as a result of death, removal or resignation of a Commissioner, a replacement of the immediate past member shall start a full term of office, provided that under no circumstances shall a person serve as a Commissioner or a Chairperson for a period exceeding nine (9) years. 16. Remuneration and Allowances of Commissioners and Staff (1) The Commissioners and the staff of the Commission shall be paid out of the funds of the Commission such remuneration, allowances and other benefits as the Commission may from time to time propose for the approval of the Governor. (2) The remuneration , allowances and other benefits of the Commissioners and the staff of the Commission shall be determined by the Commission having regard to the specialised nature of electricity regulation and the work undertaken by the Commission. 17. Code of Ethics for the Commission The Commission shall develop and issue a comprehensive Code of Ethics which shall apply to all Commissioners and staff of the Commission. 17

PART IV OBJECTIVES, FUNCTIONS, POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE COMMISSION 19. Objectives of the Commission The objectives of the Commission shall be to: (a) create, promote, facilitate and ensure an electricity market that is physically safe, technically secure, commercially sensible and economically efficient, at a reasonable cost for electricity consumers in the State; (b) ensure the optimal utilization of resources within the State for the provision of electricity services; (c) promote the deployment of environmentally friendly and climate efficient electricity solution s in the State; (d) promote the utilization of renewable energy sources by licensees, market participants, electricity consumers and other stakeholders; (e) promote the adoption of energy efficiency and demand side management in the State; (f) facilitate innovation and promote research and development in the Plateau State Electricity Market; and (g) implement such other policies, plans and programmes of the Ministry as are consistent with the provisions of this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 20. Functions of the Commission For the furtherance of the objectives of the Commiss
chunks.text: 20. Functions of the Commission For the furtherance of the objectives of the Commission, the Commission shall perform the following functions: (a) regulate generation, transmission, system operation, distribution, trading, supply and use of electricity within the State; (b) regulate, monitor and supervise the operation of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (c) licence persons engaged in the generation, transmission, system operation, distribution, trading, and supply of electricity within the State; (d) create a market framework for the Plateau State Electricity Market, which promotes and maintains efficient market behaviour; (e) prevent the misuse of market power in the Plateau State Electricity Market; 18 (f) establish and enforce appropriate operating codes and safety, security, reliability and quality standards for the Plateau State Electricity Market; (g) collect, maintain and manage electricity data and provide such data to electricity sector stakeholders in and outside the State as they may from time to time require; (h) advise the Ministry on any matter relating to the operation of this Law , including making recommendations to the Ministry for the review of policies, plans and legislation as considered appropriate or as may be requested by the Ministry; (i) collaborate generally with relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the State and Federal Government to facilitate the establishment, development, and the continual and optimal functioning of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (j) resolve disputes or complaints, issue directives and apply sanctions where necessary; (k) carry out investigations or inquiries considered necessary or desirable in connection with any matter falling within the purview of this Law; and (l) perform such other functions as may be necessary to give effect to the provisions of this Law.

chunks.text: 23. Duty to Consult for Regulations, Etc. (1) The Commission shall , prior to issuing any proposed regulation, rule, guideline or amendment, consult with licensees, electricity consumers, market participants, the House, stakeholders and other persons or groups that the Commission may consider appropriate having regard to the matters being addressed. (2) The Commission shall publish the proposed regulation, rule, guideline or amendment and relevant background materials or other information on its website and take steps to promote participation in the consultation process, including by providing for electronic access for participants or other means not requiring physical attendance. 24. Operation of Full-Service Internet Portal and Publication, Etc. (1) Before commencing operations, the Commission shall establish a full-service internet portal through which licensees, market participants, electricity consumers and other interested stakeholders may interact with the Commission, and if desired, download information on: (a) its application forms for and the terms and conditions of its various licences, permits and authorizations; (b) the activities of the Commission and regulations, guidelines, decisions, orders, directives, notices and reports issued by the Commission; (c) real-time data on all performance and quality of service standards and metrics; and (d) such other matters as may be determined by the Commission. (2) Publication of any document on the website of the Commission is effective immediately the document is on the website of the Commission.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 25. Decisions, Directives and Orders of the Commission (1) Any decision, directive o
chunks.text: 25. Decisions, Directives and Orders of the Commission (1) Any decision, directive or order given by the Commission under or for the purpose of this Law shall be in writing and shall contain the basis and reasons for the decision, directive or order. 22 (2) The decision, directive or order given by the Commission, shall be under the seal of the Commission and signed by one or more Commissioners or by an employee of the Commission duly authorized to act for that purpose. 26. Advisory Forums The Commission may constitute one or more advisory forums through which electricity consumers, licensees, market participants and other persons who have an interest in the Plateau State Electricity Market may provide advice or make recommendations in general or on a particular matter for consideration by the Commission. PART V ADMINISTRATION, MANAGEMENT AND STAFF OF THE COMMISSION 27. Administration and Management of the Commission (1) The Commissioners shall be responsible for the supervision of the activities of the Commission to ensure the proper implementation and achievement of the objectives of the Commission and the objectives of this Law. (2) The Executive Commissioners shall be responsible for day -to-day management, supervise such departments as the Commission may determine and devote their full time to the service of the Commission.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 28. Other Staff of the Commission (1) The Commission may employ such other staff as
chunks.text: 28. Other Staff of the Commission (1) The Commission may employ such other staff as it may deem necessary to assist the Commission in the performance of its functions under this Law. (2) The Commission may, subject to the provisions of this Law, make staff regulations, rules and policies relating generally to the conditions of service of the staff of the Commission. (3) The Commission may assign to its staff such functions of the Commission as the Commission deems fit. (4) The provisions of the Pension Reform Law shall be applicable to the officers, staff or employees of the Commission. (5) Nothing in subsection (4) of this section shall prevent the Commission from appointing a person to an office on terms that preclude the grant of pension or other retirement benefits in respect of that office. PART VI THE COMMISSION - FINANCIAL PROVISIONS, MONITORING AND REPORTING

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 29. Funds of the Commission (1) The Commission shall establish, maintain and control
chunks.text: 29. Funds of the Commission (1) The Commission shall establish, maintain and control a fund (referred to in this Law as “the Fund of the Commission”) from which all expenditures incurred by the Commission shall be defrayed. 23 (2) There shall be paid and credited into the Fund of the Commission: (a) the initial take-off grant made available to the Commission by the Plateau State Government; (b) all fees, levies and charges chargeable by the Commission for licences, permits, authorizations, certification, testing, inspection or any service provided by the Commission in the exercise of its functions under this Law, excluding any fines or penalties imposed and collected pursuant to this Law or regulations made by the Commission which shall be paid into the Electrification Fund; (c) all sums of money accruing to the Commission by way of grants-in-aids, gifts, testamentary dispositions, endowments and contributions from any other source provided that the condition for such grant s are not inconsistent with the objectives, functions, duties and responsibilities of the Commission under this Law; (d) fees charged for the investigation into , and resolution of all disputes brought before the Commission; and (e) all other monetary assets that may from time to time accrue to the Commission. (3) The Commission shall manage its fund in furtherance of its objectives and functions under this Law and in line with financial policies of the State.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 30. Financial Provisions (1) The Commission shall, not later than 30th September in
chunks.text: 30. Financial Provisions (1) The Commission shall, not later than 30th September in each financial year, prepare and present to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner for approval, a budget showing the estimated revenue and expenditure for the following financial year. (2) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1) of this section, the Commission may also, in any financial year, prepare and present t o the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner for approval, supplementary or adjusted statements of estimated income and expenditure. (3) Subject to subsections (1) and (2) of this section, t he Commission shall apply the Fund of the Commission: (a) to meet the administrative and operating costs of the Commission; (b) for the payment of salaries, fees, remuneration, allowances, pensions and other retirement benefits payable to the Commissioners and the staff of the Commission, as the case may be; (c) for the purchase or acquisition of property, equipment and other capital expenditure and for maintenance of any property acquired or vested in the Commission; and (d) for or in connection with all or any of the functions of the Commission under this Law or regulations made pursuant to this Law. 24 (4) One hundred percent (100%) of any amount in excess of the Commission’s revenue for any year over the approved expenditure for that year shall be paid by the Commission into the Consolidated Revenue Fund and a percentage directly into the Electrification Fund established under this Law. (5) A percentage as approved by the Governor of the amount in subsection (4) of thi s Section shall be paid into a dedicated account which shall reside with the Accountant General for the use of the Agency.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 31. Financial year of the Commission The financial year of the Commission shall comm
chunks.text: 31. Financial year of the Commission The financial year of the Commission shall commence on 1st January of each year and end on 31st December of the same year. 32. Maintenance of Proper Accounts and Records The Commission shall, in respect of each year, keep proper accounts and records in respect of all of the Commission’s activities, operations, transactions, funds and properties in accordance with the extant financial policies and guidelines of the State. 33. Audit of the Accounts and Records of the Commission (1) The Commission shall ensure that its accounts and other records kept shall be audited within three (3) months from the end of each financial year by auditors whose appointment shall be approved by the Commission provided that such auditors are on the list of auditors approved from time to time by the Auditor-General of the State. (2) The auditor shall be entitled to require to be produced all accounts and other records relating to each account which is kept by the Commission or its Commissioners, members, staff or agents and to require from any Commissioner, member, staff or agent of the Commission such information as in the auditor’s opinion are necessary for the purposes of the audit.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 34. Report of the Commission (1) The Commission shall prepare and submit to the Gove
chunks.text: 34. Report of the Commission (1) The Commission shall prepare and submit to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner annually, and to the House, not later than four (4) months after the end of its financial year, a report on the activities of the Commission for the preceding financial year and shall include the Commission’s audited accounts for the year under review together with the auditor’s report. (2) In addition to the report to be provided under subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall prepare and submit such other reports as the Honourable Commissioner may require.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 35. The Plateau State Electricity Market Report (1) The Commission shall monitor all
chunks.text: 35. The Plateau State Electricity Market Report (1) The Commission shall monitor all significant matters relating to the performance of all licensees and other market participants and publish a report titled “The Plateau State Electricity Market Report” not later than 30th April of each financial year. (2) Matters upon which the Commission shall report in the Plateau State Electricity Market R eport include: (a) the operation and administration of this Law and its regulations; 25 (b) the efficiency with which licensees and other market participants provide services to their customers; (c) the implementation of the Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan; (d) any deficiencies in the scope or operation of this Law and its regulations; and (e) Plateau State Electricity Market operations and key performance indicator surveillance data and conclusions to be drawn therefrom; and (f) other matters that the Commission is satisfied are relevant. (3) In performing its functions under subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall have regard to such industry performance indicators and reporting guidelines as the Commission has established for the Plateau State Electricity Market. (4) In preparing the Plateau State Electricity Market Report, all licensees shall be obliged to deliver all data and information that they are required to keep by regulations made hereunder and such other data and information as the Commission may require. (5) The Commission shall treat all commercially -sensitive dat a and information with the utmost confidentiality. Where a licensee believes that its interests would be adversely impacted if any of the data and information that they are required to deliver to the Commission were to be published or otherwise divulged by the Commission, the licensee shall deliver the data and information separately with each page clearly marked as “ commercially-sensitive”. The licensee shall also give reasons why the data and information are considered as commercially-sensitive. (6) The Commission shall publish the Plateau State Electricity Market Report on its website. PART VII PLANNING AND PROCUREMENT

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 36. The Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) Within six (6) months after the commenc
chunks.text: 36. The Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) Within six (6) months after the commencement of th is Law, the Commission shall in consultation with the Ministry and relevant stakeholders develop and publish the first edition of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan, which shall act as a foundational document for the establishment of the Plateau State Electricity Market. (2) The Plateau Integrated Resource Plan shall, among other things as may be necessary to meet future electricity demand in the State, consider the following matters: (a) fuel and electricity generation sources that are available within the State; (b) least cost method by which the available fuel and electricity generation sources can be deployed to meet all identified demands; 26 (c) supply and demand side resources, their potential means of deployment, the constraints to such deployment and their financial, economic and environmental impact in relation to meeting projected electricity needs; (d) reliability and security of e lectricity supply and capacity, transmission and distribution , including resilience to the effects of climate change; (e) utilization of cleaner electricity generation sources and ensuring that future electricity solutions deployed are environmentally friendly and climate efficient; (f) phasing out of environmentally damaging electricity solutions and generation sources; (g) measures relating to energy efficiency and demand side management; (h) deployment of innovative and emerging technologies; (i) ensuring that all future generation entities are designed to run on the cleanest available fuels or be derived from viable renewable energy sources; and (j) such other matters as may be necessary to ensure an orderly system for managing the procurement and deployment of a viable and sustainable electricity system for the State.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 37. Custody, Implementation and Transfer of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1)
chunks.text: 37. Custody, Implementation and Transfer of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) Prior to the establishment of the Plateau ISO, the Commission shall be responsible for the custody, review, revision, management and implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan. (2) Not later than six (6) months after commencement of operations by the Plateau ISO or such other time frame as may be agreed between the Commission and the Plateau ISO after consultation with the Honourable Commissioner, the Commission shall take all necessary steps to transfer the responsibility in respect of the custody, review, revis ion, management and implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan to the Plateau ISO.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 38. Monitoring the Revision, Management and Implementation of the Plateau Integrated
chunks.text: 38. Monitoring the Revision, Management and Implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) The Commission shall be responsible for regulating and monitoring the overall revision, management and implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan by the Plateau ISO and may: (a) issue directive s to the Plateau ISO setting out the requirements for the revision, management and implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan; and (b) require the Plateau ISO to submit to the Commission , a plan containing an outline of the steps the Plateau ISO intends to take: (i) in connection with the revision, management and implementation of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan; and (ii) to meet the requirements set out in any directive issued by the Commission. (2) The Commission shall review every plan submitted by the Plateau ISO and shall: 27 (a) approve the plan, with or without changes; or (b) reject the plan providing detailed comments and reasons for its decision and return the plan to the Plateau ISO for further consideration and re-submission to the Commission. (3) The Plateau ISO shall provide an annual report to the Commission, within the time specified by the Commission, setting out the steps that have been taken to implement the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan, progress made and such other matters as may be required by the Commission or as the Plateau ISO considers advisable.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 39. Duration, Review and Publication of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) Eac
chunks.text: 39. Duration, Review and Publication of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan (1) Each edition of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan shall be set over a planning time frame of not less than ten (10) years, but shall be subject to a comprehensive review no later than every five (5) years following the publication of the first edition. (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1) of this section, the Plateau ISO may, from time to time as it deems necessary, after consultation with the Commission , review and revise the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan. (3) The Plateau Integrated Resource Plan and any revision shall be published on the website of the Commission and the Plateau ISO.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 40. Framework for Procurement of Electricity and Ancillary Services (1) The developm
chunks.text: 40. Framework for Procurement of Electricity and Ancillary Services (1) The development of new electricity supply sources , all contracts for the purchase of electricity and ancillary services and all activities required to be carried out under the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan in relation to the Plateau State Electricity Market shall be awarded in accordance with an open, transparent and competitive procurement framework issued by the Commission. (2) The Public Procurement Law of the State or any replacement or amendment of the same shall apply to procurements by the Commission, excluding the purchase of electricity and ancillary services pursuant to subsection (1) of this section. (3) The Plateau ISO shall be responsible for the management and implementation of the competitive procurement framework issued by the Commission pursuant to subsection (1) of this section. (4) Prior to the establishment of the Plateau ISO, the Commission shall take responsibility for the management and implementation of the competitive procurement framework issued by it pursuant to subsection (1) of this section. (5) Not later than six (6) months after commencement of operations by the Plateau ISO or such other time frame as may be agreed between the Commission and the Plateau ISO after consultation with the Honourable Commissioner, the Commission shall take all necessary steps to transfer the responsibility for the management and implementation of the competitive procurement framework to the Plateau ISO. PART VIII ELECTRICITY LICENCES – GENERAL PROVISIONS 28

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 41. Restriction on Electricity Services without Licence (1) No person shall construc
chunks.text: 41. Restriction on Electricity Services without Licence (1) No person shall construct, own or operate any undertaking or in any way engage in: (a) the generation of electricity; (b) the transmission of electricity; (c) the distribution of electricity; (d) the trading of electricity; (e) the supply of electricity; (f) system operation; or (g) the provision of such other activit ies or services relating to electricity as the Commission may, by regulations, specify in the State, except in accordance with a licence granted by the Commission pursuant to this Law or deemed to have been granted under Part XIX of this Law, or the person is exempted under this Part. (2) Any person who contravenes subsection (1) of this section commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not less than One Million Naira (N1,000,000.00) or imprisonment for a term not less than three (3) months or to both such fine and imprisonment. In the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine not less than Five Thousand Naira (N5,000.00) for every day or part thereof during which the offence continues after conviction. (3) The Commission may, through a fair, open and competitive process in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Commission by regulations, invite applications from credible and capable entities for the provision of services in the Plateau State Electricity Market pursuant to a licence to be issued by the Commission under this Law. (4) Where a person is uncertain as to whether he is engaging, or is about to engage in a n undertaking or activity for which a licence is required pursuant to the provision of subsection (1) of this section, the person shall seek clarification and clearance from the Commission. (5) The Commission may, by regulation , prescribe additional activities to be undertaken only on the basis of a licence or permit and shall have the power to issue licences or permits for such activities in accordance with this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 42. Exemptions (1) The Commission may, by regulation, exempt any person from the req
chunks.text: 42. Exemptions (1) The Commission may, by regulation, exempt any person from the requirement to obtain a licence pursuant to section 41 of this Law: (a) generally or to such an extent as may be specified in the regulation; (b) unconditionally or subject to such conditions as may be specified in the regulation; and (c) subject to such other terms and conditions as the Commission may specify. 29 (2) If any term or condition of an exemption granted pursuant to subsection (1) of this section is not complied with by any person, the Commission may direct that the subject exemption be revoked, and the process set out in section 49 of this Law shall apply.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 43. Application for Grant and Refusal of Licences (1) An application for a licence s
chunks.text: 43. Application for Grant and Refusal of Licences (1) An application for a licence shall be made to the Commission in such form and manner, and shall contain, or be accompanied by such information and documents and such fee as may be prescribed in regulations made by the Commission. (2) Subject to subsection (3) of this section, t he Commission may grant an appropriate licence, to an applicant if on consideration of an application, the Commission is satisfied that: (a) the applicant satisfies the requirements set out in any regulation made by the Commission; (b) the applicant will comply with such provisions of this Law, including, without limitation, all regulations, guidelines , orders, codes of conduct, standards and licence terms and conditions as may be applicable to the undertaking , service, activity or system it intends to construct, own, operate or provide; and (c) the grant of the licence is in the public interest. (3) If on consideration of an application, the Commission is not satisfied as to the matters referred to in subsection (2) of this section, the Commission may refuse to grant a licence to the applicant provided that before refusing to grant the licence, the Commission shall: (a) notify the applicant in writing that it proposes to refuse the application; (b) set out in the notice referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection, its reasons for proposing the refusal of the application; (c) afford the applicant an adequate opportunity to make representations in respect of the matter and show cause why the licence should be granted; (d) consider any r epresentations made by the applicant pursuant to paragraph (c) of this subsection; and (e) where practicable, provide the applicant adequate opportunity to address any issues identified by the Commission. (4) The period between the Commission’s receipt of an application and the date the Commission notifies the applicant of its decision or proposed decision in accordance with subsection (2) or (3) of this section, as the case may be, shall not exceed three (3) months from the date the application is received as complete by the Commission.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 44. Terms and Conditions of Licences (1) A licence granted by the Commission shall b
chunks.text: 44. Terms and Conditions of Licences (1) A licence granted by the Commission shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be reasonably determined by the Commission. 30 (2) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1) of this section, the terms and conditions of a licence shall be contained in a license agreement to be executed between the Commission and the licensee and may require the licensee to: (a) enter into agreements on specified terms with other persons for the provision of access to or use of electric lines , plants, system and associated equipment owned, controlled or operated by the licensee; (b) comply with directions to ensure efficient market behaviour in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (c) take steps to promote and support research and development activities; (d) comply with energy efficiency and demand side management practices, standards and requirements; (e) take steps to support and facilitate the provision of off-grid solutions; (f) observe certain obligations with regard s to the dismantling or removal of any installations , equipment and structures and in respect of waste disposal, including e-waste; (g) resolve disputes by means of alternative dispute resolution method; (h) file appeals against the decisions, directions, orders, determinations or rulings of t he Commission to the High Court; (i) pay a periodic fee to the Commission during the currency of the licence; (j) educate electricity consumers of their rights and responsibilities; (k) ensure that contracts executed by the licensee in connection with or related to its licensed activities are subject to alternative dispute resolution rules; (l) obtain the consent of the Commission prior to any transaction that may, whether directly or indirectly, alter the shareholding structure of the licensee; (m) prior to commencing operations, establish a full -service internet portal through which the Commission, its stakeholders or other interested persons may interact with it, and if desired, download information on: (i) its service offerings, relevant forms for applying for them and their respective terms and conditions; (ii) applicable tariffs, customer care standards

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 45. Modification of Terms and Conditions (1) The Commission may, at any time, modify
chunks.text: 45. Modification of Terms and Conditions (1) The Commission may, at any time, modify the terms and conditions of a licence in accordance with any regulation prescribed for that purpose. (2) A modification of the terms and conditions of a licence may be initiated: (a) by the concerned licensee; (b) by the Commission, on its own initiative; or (c) pursuant to a complaint from any other licensee, electricity consumer or other market participants. (3) The Commission shall not modify any term or condition of a licence unless it is satisfied that the modification is requisite or expedient having regard to the objectives and functions of the Commission and the objectives of this Law. (4) Before making any modification to the terms and conditions of a licence, the Commission shall give notice by publication on its website: (a) stating that it proposes to make a modification in the manner specified in the notice; 32 (b) stating the reasons why the Commission proposes to make the modification, including whether the need for the modification was the subject of a prior representation made by the concerned licensee, a third party or based on the Commission’s own initiative; (c) specifying the period from the date of the giving of the notice (not being less than one (1) month) within which written objections or representations with respect to the proposed modification may be made to the Commission; and (d) the address to which the written objections or representations may be sent. (5) Where the Commission receives any written objection or representation, the Commission shall not modify the terms and conditions of the licence until all such objections or representations have been duly considered and determined by the Commission. (6) If no written objection or representation is received by the Commission within the period specified pursuant to subsection (4)(c) of this section or if any written objection or representation made under that subsection is subsequently withdrawn, the Commission may forthwith carry out the modification as specified in the notice given under subsection (4) of this section.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 46. Duration of Licences A licence shall be valid for the period prescribed by the C
chunks.text: 46. Duration of Licences A licence shall be valid for the period prescribed by the Commission and stated in the licence, provided that the period of a licence or any renewal granted by the Commission shall not be more than ten (10) years.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 47. Renewal of Licences (1) Subject to the provisions of this Law, a licen see may a
chunks.text: 47. Renewal of Licences (1) Subject to the provisions of this Law, a licen see may apply for a renewa l of its licence before the expiration of the licence. Where a licensee submits its application for a renewal after the expiration of the licence, such licensee shall show cause as to why the applica tion should be considered by the Commission. (2) An application for a renewal of a licence shall be made to the Commission in such form and manner, and shall contain, or be accompanied by, such information and documents and such fee as may be prescribed in regulations made by the Commission. (3) The Commission shall renew a licence where it is satisfied that the licensee: (a) is not in breach of any of the terms and conditions of the licence; (b) is in compliance with all the obligations imposed on the licence under this Law or any other subsidiary legislation made by the Commission or has satisfactorily taken or is taking steps to be in compliance therewith; and (c) continues to meet the requirements for the issuance of the licence. (4) If on consideration of an application for renewal, the Commission is not satisfied as to the matters referred to in subsection (3) of this section, the Commission sh all refuse to renew the licence provided that before refusing to renew the licence, the Commission shall: (a) notify the applicant in writing that it proposes to refuse the renewal of the application; 33 (b) set out in the notice referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection, its reasons for proposing the refusal of the renewal application; (c) afford the applicant an adequate opportunity to make representations in respect of the matter and show cause why the licence should be renewed; (d) consider any representa tions made by the applicant pursuant to paragraph (c) of this subsection; and (e) where practicable, provide the applicant an adequate opportunity to address any issues identified by the Commission.
