chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 48. Restriction on Transfer of Licence (1) No licence shall be disposed, assigned, n
chunks.text: 48. Restriction on Transfer of Licence (1) No licence shall be disposed, assigned, novated , or howsoever transferred, whether directly or indirectly and whether by way of sale, acquisition of shares, merger, mortgage, charge, pledge, lease, franchise or otherwise, without the prior approval in writing of the Commission. (2) Any purported transfer , assignment, novation or disposal of a licence without the approval of the Commission as required under subsection (1) of this section shall be void.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 49. Withdrawal, Suspension or Revocation of Licences The Commission may withdraw, su
chunks.text: 49. Withdrawal, Suspension or Revocation of Licences The Commission may withdraw, suspend or revoke a licence where: (a) the Commission is satisfied that the licence was procured through misrepresentation or nondisclosure of a material fact by the licensee; (b) a court of competent jurisdiction declares that the licence was issued through fraud or contrary to corrupt practices and money laundering laws applicable in the State; (c) the Commission is satisfied that the licensee is either willfully or negligently not operating in accordance with the terms and conditions of the licence, or the provisions of this Law or any regulations made hereunder; 34 (d) the Commission is satisfied that the licensee had either willfully or unreasonably contravened any provisions of this Law or any regulations made hereunder; (e) the licensee has failed to comply with any term or condition of the licence, the breach of which is expressly declared by such licence to render it liable to suspension or revocation; (f) the Commission is satisfied that the licensee no longer has the financial wherewithal to fully and efficiently perform the duties and obligations imposed by the licence; (g) the licensee is declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be insolvent or bankrupt; (h) the licensee fails to comply with any milestones pursuant to whi ch the licence was issued; or (i) the licensee has not commenced operations within any period specified in the licence or in any applicable regulations

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 50. Procedure for Withdrawal, Suspension or Revocation of Licences (1) Before withdr
chunks.text: 50. Procedure for Withdrawal, Suspension or Revocation of Licences (1) Before withdrawing, suspending or revoking a licence, the Commission shall notify the licensee in writing, including by publication on its website, stating: (a) its intention to withdraw, suspend or revoke the licence; (b) its reasons for proposing the withdrawal, suspension or revocation of the licence; (c) the applicable grounds pursuant to which the Commission is proposing to withdraw, suspend or revoke the licence as provided under this Law; and (d) a maximum timeframe, not being less than fourteen (14) days following the date of delivery of the notification to the licensee, within which the licensee shall be allowed to: (i) make representations and show cause wh y the licence should not be withdrawn, suspended or revoked; and (ii) take steps to remedy the situation that gave rise to the proposed withdrawal, suspension or revocation. (2) Where the Commission is satisfied with the representations made or the remedy provided by the licensee pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the process for withdrawal, suspension or revocation of the licence shall terminate. (3) Where upon the expiration of the time frame provided to the Licensee pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the Commission is satisfied based on any of the grounds provided under this Law that the licence should be withdrawn, suspended or revoked, the Commission may , by notice in writing to the licensee, which notice shall also be published on its website, and without any compensation: (a) withdraw the licence; or (b) suspend the licence and prescribe actions to be taken by the licensee for the suspension to be lifted; or 35 (c) revoke the licence; or (d) appoint a competent person to operate the undertaking and prescribe remedial actions that may be taken by the licensee to have the undertaking restored to it; (e) allow the licence to remain in force, subject to such further terms and conditions as it ma y deem necessary to impose, which terms and conditions shall form part of the licence; or (f) take such other action as it considers appropriate. (4) The withdrawal, suspension or revocation of a licence shall not pr

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 51. Separation between each Business Segment (1) The Commission may require a licens
chunks.text: 51. Separation between each Business Segment (1) The Commission may require a licensee to implement management, accounting or legal separation in respect of its licensed or permitted activities, which may prevent the licensee from directly holding licences of another type. (2) A licensee shall not, without the prior written approval of the Commission, directly or indirectly acquire or otherwise obtain an interest in, or have an interest acquired in it or affiliate or merge with another licensee or an affiliate of a licensee. (3) In providing its approval pursuant to subsection (2) of this section , the Commission may impose conditions to be satisfied by the parties.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 52. Enforcement (1) Without derogating from the powers conferred on the Commission p
chunks.text: 52. Enforcement (1) Without derogating from the powers conferred on the Commission pursuant to section 49 and 50 of this Law, where the Commission is satisfied that a licensee or any market participant is contravening, or is likely to contravene or has contravened any: (a) term or condition of its licence; 36 (b) code, rule, performance standard , manual, guideline or other standard applicable to the licensee; (c) direction issued by the Commission to or applicable to the licensee; or (d) provision of this Law or regulation made hereunder; the Commission may serve upon the licensee an order (which order shall also be published on its website) to do one or more of the things set out in subsection (2) of this section. (2) Pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the Commission may by order: (a) direct the licensee to do or not do such things as are specified in such order and stipulate the applicable timeframe for compliance; (b) require the licensee to provide any form of security on such terms and conditions as the Commission may determine; (c) require the licensee to implement any measures as are specified in such order and stipulate the applicable timeframe for the implementation; or (d) specify a penalty for each day that the licensee is in default of compliance with the order, which shall not be less than Five Thousand Naira (N5,000.00) for each such day. (3) Before serving an order on the licensee pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall notify the licensee in writing (including by publication on its website) stating: (a) its intention to issue an order in terms of subsection (2) of this section to the licensee; (b) the grounds upon which the order is to be issued; (c) the measures the Commission considers reasonably necessary for the purpose of rectifying or avoiding any contravention or threatened contravention that may give rise to the proposed order; (d) a maximum timeframe, not being less than fourteen (14) days following the date of delivery of the notification to the licensee, within which the licensee shall be allowed to: (i) make representations to the Commission; and (ii) implement any measures proposed by the Commission

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 53. Licensing Regulations (1) Subject to the provisions of this Law, the Commission
chunks.text: 53. Licensing Regulations (1) Subject to the provisions of this Law, the Commission shall by regulation prescribe the form, manner and procedure of all licensing matters, including in respect of application, grant, refusal, renewal, modification, transfer, assignme nt, suspension, withdrawal, revocation, enforcement, applicable fees, documentary and information requirements, or other special terms and conditions relating to a licence as the Commission may deem necessary. (2) The Commission shall make the regulations req uired pursuant to subsection (1) of this s ection in such a manner as to: (a) simplify, expedite and automate the application and licensing process; (b) impose minimal costs on applicants and licensees; (c) facilitate ease of entry into the Plateau State Electricity Market; (d) encourage innovation and investments in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (e) ensure that public notice of any application for a licence is widely given across the State and all objections and representations received by the Commission are considered and determined; (f) promote efficient market behaviour in the Plateau State Electricity Market and protect the interests of electricity consumers and the general public; (g) ensure that applicants and licensees are well funded and managed and have the requisite technical capacity to operate in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (h) ensure transparency, fairness and non-discrimination; and (i) ensure the protection of the environment.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 54. Publication and Register of Licences (1) The Commission shall publish a notice o
chunks.text: 54. Publication and Register of Licences (1) The Commission shall publish a notice of its decision to grant, renew, modify, suspend, cancel, withdraw or revoke a licence on its website and in the form and manner as may be prescribed in any regulation issued by the Commission. (2) The Commission shall, in such form as it may determine, estab lish and maintain a register for the purposes of entering into the register the provisions of: (a) every licence granted, renewed, withdrawn, modified, suspended, revoked or expired; (b) every exemption granted; 38 (c) every direction, order, consent or authorization given or any determination made with respect to a licence; and (d) such other information or matters as the Commission may consider necessary, provided that the Commission may exclude the details of any provisions from the register if in the opinion of the Commission it is necessary to exclude such provisions to protect the public interest or the commercial interests of any person. (3) The Commission shall publish the contents of the register on its website. (4) A member of the public may, upon the payment of prescribed fees, require the Commission to supply him with a certified true copy of any document, record, extract from or any part of the register.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 55. Default Approvals (1) Any matter which requires the Commission’s approval under
chunks.text: 55. Default Approvals (1) Any matter which requires the Commission’s approval under this Law or under any regulation, shall be approved or refused within the specified time limit. (2) Where no time limit is specified under this Law or in any applicable regulation, the time limit referred to in subsection (1) of this section shall be four (4) months. (3) Where t he Commission accepts or rejects an application , it shall within the specified time limit communicate its decision to the applicant and an accurate record of it shall be kept. PART IX GENERATION LICENCES 56. Grant of a Generation Licence The Commission may grant a licence authorizing a person to engage in the generation of electricity within the State in accordance with this Law and any regulations made hereunder (“a generation licence”). 57. Activities under a Generation Licence Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may prescribe in the generation licence and compliance with the provisions of this Law and any regulations made hereunder, a generation licence may authorize the holder to: (a) construct, own, operate and maintain a generating station for the purposes of the generation and provision of electricity as specified in the licence; (b) sell electricity or provide ancillary services as specified in the licence; and (c) where applicable, connect to a transmission system, distribution system or any electricity system for dispatch.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 58. Service Obligations of a Generation Licensee A generation licensee shall: 39 (a)
chunks.text: 58. Service Obligations of a Generation Licensee A generation licensee shall: 39 (a) develop, operate and maintain a reliable, efficient, safe, economical and environmentally responsible system of electricity generation in accordance with applicable rules, codes, standards etc. as may be issued or approved by the Commission; (b) co-ordinate with other licensees and market participants as the circumstances may require; and (c) as a market participant, comply fully with all instructions/directions of the Plateau ISO given under the Market Rules and grid code, howsoever called. PART X TRANSMISSION LICENCES 59. Grant of a Transmission Licence The Commission may grant a licence authorizing a person to engage in the transmission of electricity within the State in accordance with this Law and any regulations made hereunder (“a transmission licence”).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 60. Activities Under a Transmission Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions
chunks.text: 60. Activities Under a Transmission Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may prescribe in the transmission licence and compliance with the provisions of this Law or any regulations made hereunder, a transmission licence may authorize the holder to: (a) construct, own, operate and maintain a transmission system within the State; and (b) connect its transmission system to another transmission system or a distribution system or any electricity system within the State grid or to the national grid or the grid of any other State as specified in the licence. (2) The grant of a transmission licence shall not limit the power of the Commission to grant a licence of similar purpose to another person: Provided that the Commission may grant exclusive transmission licence for all or part of the period of the transmission licence for a specific purpose or geographical area or both.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 61. Service Obligations of a Transmission Licensee A transmission licensee shall: (a
chunks.text: 61. Service Obligations of a Transmission Licensee A transmission licensee shall: (a) develop, operate and maintain a reliable, efficient, safe, economical and environmentally responsible transmission system in accordance with applicable rules, codes, standards etc. as may be issued or approved by the Commission; (b) provide non-discriminatory access to its transmission system for use by any licensee or market participant in accordance with this Law, the terms and conditions of its licence and applicable rules and regulations; (c) publicly make available its rates, charges and other terms and conditions as applicable to its services; 40 (d) co-ordinate with other licensees and market participants as the circumstances may require; and (e) as a market participant, comply fully with all instructions and directions of the Plateau ISO given under the Market Rules and grid code, howsoever called. PART XI DISTRIBUTION LICENCES 62. Grant of a Distribution Licence The Commission may grant a licence authorizing a person to engage in the distribution of electricity within the State in accordance with this Law and any regulations made hereunder (“a distribution licence”).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 63. Activities Under a Distribution Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions
chunks.text: 63. Activities Under a Distribution Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may prescribe in the distribution licence and compliance with the provisions of this Law or any regulations made hereunder, a distribution licence may authorize the holder to: (a) construct, own, operate and maintain a distribution system within the State; and (b) connect its distribution system to a transmission system, distribution system or any electricity system within the State as specified in the licence. (2) The grant of a distribution licence shall not limit the power of the Commission to grant a licence of similar purpose to another person : Provided that the Commission may grant exclusive distribution licence for all or part of the period of the distribution licence for a specific purpose or geographical area or both.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 64. Service Obligations of a Distribution Licensee A distribution licensee shall: (a
chunks.text: 64. Service Obligations of a Distribution Licensee A distribution licensee shall: (a) develop, operate and maintain a reliable, efficient, safe, economical and environmentally responsible distribution system in accordance with applicable rules, codes, standards etc. as may be issued or approved by the Commission; (b) provide non-discriminatory access to its distribution system for use by any licensee or market participant in accordance with this Law, the terms and conditions of its licence and applicable rules; (c) publicly make available its rates, charges and other terms and conditions as applicable to its services; (d) co-ordinate with other licensees and market participants as the circumstances may require; and (e) as a market participant, comply fully with all instructions/directions of the Plateau ISO given under the Market Rules and grid code, howsoever called. PART XII SUPPLY LICENCES 41 65. Grant of a Supply Licence The Commission may grant a licence authorizing a person to engage in the provision of a specific supply service within the State in accordance with this Law and any regulations made hereunder (a “supply licence”).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 66. Activities Under a Supply Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions as th
chunks.text: 66. Activities Under a Supply Licence (1) Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may prescribe in the licence and compliance with the provisions of this Law or any r egulations made hereunder, a supply licence holder may be authorized to provide one (1) or more of the following services as ma y be specified in the licence: (a) engage in the purchasing, selling and/or trading of electricity or ancillary services; (b) enter into appropriate agreements with a transmission licensee or a distribution licensee for wheeling of electricity; (c) purchase electricity and/or ancillary services for supply to electricity consumers; (d) supply of electricity to electricity consumers; (e) connect electricity consumers for the purposes of receiving supply of electricity; (f) supply, install, maintain or read meters for the purpose of billing and collection of revenue; or (g) undertake such other activities or provide such other services as may be prescri bed in the licence. (2) The Commission may issue a separate licence for each of the activities mentioned in subsection (1) of this section. (3) The Commission in granting the supply licence shall expressly specify in the licence the nature of the services that the licensee is authorized to provide. (4) The grant of a supply licence shall not limit the power of the Commission to grant a licence of similar purpose to another person: Provided that the Commission may grant exclusive supply licence for all or part of the period of the supply licence for a specific purpose or geographical area or both.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 67. Service Obligations of a Supply Licensee A supply licensee shall, having regard
chunks.text: 67. Service Obligations of a Supply Licensee A supply licensee shall, having regard to the nature of the authorized activities as specified in the licence: (a) engage in the trading of electricity and/or ancillary services on a non -discriminatory basis in accordance with this Law, the terms and conditions of its licence and applicable rules and regulations; (b) publicly make available its rates, charges and other terms and conditions as applicable to its services; (c) provide quality service to electricity consumers and ensure that all its transactions are transparent; (d) facilitate timely and effective billing, collection and dissemination of payments; 42 (e) supply electricity to electricity consumers on a non-discriminatory basis in accordance with this Law, the terms and conditions of its licence and applicable rules; (f) publicly make available its rates, charges and other terms and conditions as applicable to its services; (g) co-ordinate with other licensees and market participants as the circumstances may require; (h) develop, operate and maintain a reliable, efficient, safe, economical and environmentally responsible business in accordance with applicable rules, codes, standards etc. as may be issued or approved by the Commission; and (i) as a market participant, comply fully with all instructions/directions of the Plateau ISO given under the Market Rules and grid code, howsoever called. PART XIII THE PLATEAU ISO

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 68. Formation and Structure of the Plateau ISO (1) The Commission shall: (a) not lat
chunks.text: 68. Formation and Structure of the Plateau ISO (1) The Commission shall: (a) not later than eighteen (18) months after the commencement of this Law or such later time as the Honourable Commissioner may approve; and (b) after consultations with the Honourable Commissioner and relevant stakeholders, take such necessary steps to establish the Plateau ISO and issue a system operation licence to the Plateau ISO. (2) Subject to compliance with subsection (1)(b) of this section, for the purposes of the establishment, operation and functioning of the Plateau ISO, the Commission shall by means of rules prescribe: (a) the corporate structure of the Plateau ISO; (b) the initial funding and assets of the Plateau ISO; (c) the persons or class of persons qualified to be initial members of the Plateau ISO; (d) the composition of and the procedure for nominating the initial members of the governing body of the Plateau ISO; or (e) any ancillary, administrative or procedural matter that is necessary to prescribe for the proper implementation and administration of the Plateau ISO. (3) In the event of any inconsistency between the constitutional documents establishing and governing the management of the Plateau ISO and this Law or any applicable regulations, rules, guidelines etc. issued by the Commission , this Law or such regulations, rules, guidelines etc. shall prevail to the extent of the inconsistency. (4) In the establishment, operation and functioning of the Plateau ISO, the Commission shall ensure that: 43 (a) the Plateau ISO is structured as a not-for-profit entity owned by qualified licensed entities in the Plateau State Electricity Market on a mutualized and non-discriminatory basis and financially independent of all market participants, capital providers and other stakeholders in the Plateau State Electricity Market and other electricity markets in Nigeria; (b) any profit made by the Plateau ISO is not distributed to its members but utilized by the Plateau ISO for the purpose of carrying out its objects; (c) no single member or group of members dominate or influence the administration and operational decisions of the Plateau ISO; and (d) the Plateau ISO is independent

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 69. Activities of the Plateau ISO Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commis
chunks.text: 69. Activities of the Plateau ISO Subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may prescribe in the system operation licence issued to the Plateau ISO pursuant to this Law and in compliance with the provisions of this Law and any regulations made hereunder, the system operation licence shall authorize the Plateau ISO to carry out the following activities with the sole objective of ensuring and maintaining reliability of supply in the Plateau State Electricity Market: (a) generation scheduling, commitment and dispatch; (b) transmission scheduling; (c) generation outage co-ordination; (d) transmission congestion management; (e) procurement and scheduling of ancillary services; (f) administration of the wholesale electricity market in the State, including its trading and settlements systems; (g) carry out the responsibilities placed on the system operator in respect of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan; (h) manage the connection of the State grid with the national grid or the electricity system of any other State; (i) conduct such other activities as may be required to direct the reliable and efficient operation of the State grid; 44 (j) carry out any other functions that may be prescribed under the Market Rules, this Law or any regulation made by the Commission.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 70. Service Obligations of the Plateau ISO The Plateau ISO shall: (a) perform its fu
chunks.text: 70. Service Obligations of the Plateau ISO The Plateau ISO shall: (a) perform its functions and exercise its powers in a manner that is open , fair, reasonable, objective, non-discriminatory and conducive to efficient market behaviour in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (b) ensure that its operations are conducted in such a manner as to facilitate non -discriminatory treatment of licensees and market participants; (c) ensure that information in relation to its activities are provided on an equal basis and in the same manner to all licensees and market participants; and (d) exercise and perform such powers and duties assigned to it under the Market Rules.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 71. The Market Rules (1) The Plateau ISO shall be responsible for the development an
chunks.text: 71. The Market Rules (1) The Plateau ISO shall be responsible for the development and modification of the Market Rules for the safe, reliable and efficient operati on of the State electricity system, governing the activities of and relationships between licensees and market participants, and for the establishment and governance of markets related to electricity and ancillary services. (2) The Plateau ISO shall ensure that the Market Rules made or modified are published in such manner as will ensure adequate publicity, including by publication on its website. (3) The Market Rules developed by the Plateau ISO and any modification shall be subject to the prior review and approval of the Commission. (4) The Market Rules and any modification thereof shall have the effect of a contract between each licensee/market participant and the Plateau ISO pursuant to which each licensee/market participant and the Plateau ISO respectively agree to perform and observe the terms and conditions of the Market Rules. PART XIV TARIFF REGULATION

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 72. General Tariff Regulation (1) Activities licensed by the Commission pursuant to
chunks.text: 72. General Tariff Regulation (1) Activities licensed by the Commission pursuant to this Law or any regulation shall be subject to one or more tariff methodologies and for such period as may be adopted by the Commission in accordance with this Law. (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1) of this section, the Commission may, subject to compliance with such terms and conditions as may be prescribed by the Commission and in accordance with a relevant tariff methodology established by the Commission, approve: 45 (a) any willing-seller and willing -buyer arrangement (including the tariffs and charges agreed pursuant to that arrangement) between a licensee and a class or classes of electricity consumers; and (b) tariffs and charges that reflect the terms of any contract between licensees.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 73. Principles Guiding Tariff Methodologies Any tariff methodology adopted by the Co
chunks.text: 73. Principles Guiding Tariff Methodologies Any tariff methodology adopted by the Commission pursuant to this Part of this Law shall be based on the following principles: (a) ensure open, transparent and competitive generation procurement processes; (b) ensure a consistent and a political response to macroeconomic signals; (c) allow an efficient licensee to recover the full and reasonable costs incurred in conducting its business activities and a reasonable return on the capital invested in the business; (d) promote continued investments by licensees; (e) ensure the efficiency of the business and discourage wasteful expenditure; (f) ensure the continued improvement of the quality of service; (g) encourage willing -buyer and willing -seller transactions in every se gment of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (h) encourage competition in the Plateau State Electricity Market; (i) where feasible, avoid cross-subsidies among different categories of electricity consumers; (j) provide clear and accurate information to electricity consumers in relation to the costs that their consumption imposes on the licensee’s business and encourage efficient electricity consumption; (k) fairness and avoidance of undue discrimination between electricity consumers, provided that a tariff methodology adopted by the Commission may: (i) differentiate among electricity consumers on the basis of differences in total electricity consumption, the time periods at which electricity is consumed, load factors, power factors, voltage levels, location and such other criteria that may affect the cost of providing a service; and (ii) allow a lifeline tariff for specific electricity consumers identified by simple transparent criteria; (l) promote innovation and the adoption of clean and modern technology; and (m) promote the use of the cleanest available electricity generation sources.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 74. Procedure for Adoption of Tariff Methodology 46 (1) The Commission shall, p rior
chunks.text: 74. Procedure for Adoption of Tariff Methodology 46 (1) The Commission shall, p rior to adopting a tariff methodology or amending an existing tariff methodology, consult with licensees, electricity consumers, market participants, stakeholders and other persons or groups that the Commission may consider appropriate considering the subject of the proposed tariff methodology. (2) Prior to holding the consultation process pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall, as may be applicable, publish in at least two (2) newspapers with wide coverage in the State and on its website, notice of: (a) the consultation process and invitation to participate in the consultation; (b) the venue and period during which the consultation is to be held , provided that the notice period for the commencement of the consultation process shall not be less than twenty-one (21) (c) the nature of the matter to which the consultation relates; and (d) the matters upon which the Commission would require submissions, the form in which submissions are to take and the address to which the submissions may be sent. (3) The Commission shall take steps to promote partic ipation in the consultation process, including by publishing any relevant background materials or other information on its website and providing for electronic access for participants or other means not requiring physical attendance. (4) The Commission may, in adopting a tariff methodology or any amendment, take into consideration the results of and any submissions made during the consultation process pursuant to subsection (1) of this section. (5) The Commission shall fix the date on which the adopted tariff methodology or any amendment shall come into effect and shall cause notice of the effective date to be published in at least two (2) newspapers with wide coverage in the State and on its website.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 75. Tariffs and Charges by Licensees (1) Every licensee or market participant under
chunks.text: 75. Tariffs and Charges by Licensees (1) Every licensee or market participant under obligation to set tariffs and charges shall be bound by the tariff methodology and any amendment of the same adopted by the Commission. (2) The Commission shall by regulation set out the process for approving tariffs and charges proposed by licensees. (3) Any licensee who exceeds the tariff rates approved by the Commission or imposes unapproved tariffs and charges for the provision of any of its services commits an offence under this Law. (4) The Commission shall by regulations prescribe appropriate sanctions , including the imposition of financial penalties upon any licensee who commits an offence pursuant to s ubsection (1) of this section. 76. Publication of Tariff Methodology, Tariffs and Charges (1) The Commission shall publish adopted tariff methodology on its website. 47 (2) All licensees shall publish all tariff and charges applicable to their respective services and any amendment or modification on their website. PART XV MARKET REGULATION, INDUSTRY STANDARDS AND CODES, AND CONSUMER AFFAIRS

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 77. Market Regulation (1) The Commission shall have the ongoing responsibility of mo
chunks.text: 77. Market Regulation (1) The Commission shall have the ongoing responsibility of monitoring the state of the Plateau State Electricity Market and market behaviour of licensees and other market participants. (2) Without limiting the generality of the provisions of subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall in particular have the responsibility to: (a) ensure the development and maintenance of a commercially sensible and economically efficient market; (b) prevent and address any discriminatory conduct in the market or practices inimical to the efficient functioning of the market; and (c) remove and address any arrangements that stifle competition in the Market. (3) In the performance of its responsibilities pursuant to subsection (1) of this section, the Commission shall be entitled to: (a) require and compel the disclosure of information and provision of documents by licensees and other market participants; (b) undertake such inquiries and investigations as it may consider necessary; (c) retain an independent entity to provide market monitoring and surveillance services; and (d) take such actions as may be necessary for the effective discharge of the responsibilities of the Commission. (4) Where the Commission determines that there is or may be any circumstances which distorts the efficiency of the Plateau State Electricity Market or adversely impacts its operations, the Commission may: (a) issue cease orders as may be required; (b) levy fines as may be prescribed by regulations issued by the Commission; and (c) give directions to such persons as the Commission considers appropriate. (5) The Commission shall consider the responsibilities imposed on it under subsection (1) of this section in its decisions, orders and determinations regarding matters such as, but not limited to, licence applications, grant of licence, licence terms and conditions, and tariff methodology. (6) The Commission may issue guidelines in order to provide certainty in relation to any one or more of the provisions in this section and may consult with such persons as it considers appropriate for the purpose of preparing such guidelines under this subsection. 48 (7) Parties to any a

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 78. Industry Standards and Codes (1) The Commission shall, in consultation with lice
chunks.text: 78. Industry Standards and Codes (1) The Commission shall, in consultation with licensees, market participants and such other stakeholders or interested parties that the Commission may consider appropriate, make and issue standards, codes and manuals in relation to: (a) the administration and operation of the Plateau State Electricity Market; (b) the activities of licensees and market participants; (c) the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the electricity system in the State; (d) the provision of electricity equipment, facilities and instruments, including requirements for qualified providers and installers; (e) the promotion of energy efficiency and deman d side management practices by licence es and electricity consumers; (f) quality of service, service standards and performance standards; (g) the safe, reliable and efficient interconnection of the Plateau State Electricity Market with the national electricity market; and (h) such other matters as the Commission may consider appropriate as is necessary or expedient to achieve or promote the objectives of this Law. (2) The standards, codes and manuals issued by the Commission pursuant to subsection (1) of this section shall be published by the Commission on its website.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 79. Consumer Protection Standards, Practices and Procedures (1) The Commission shall
chunks.text: 79. Consumer Protection Standards, Practices and Procedures (1) The Commission shall issue regulations and any amendments setting out standards, practices and procedures for the protection of electricity consumers in the State, including but not limited to the following matters: (a) service standards, including the establishment of special services for disadvantaged consumers; (b) complaint handling standards and resolution procedures; (c) procedures for applying for and withdrawal of electricity services; (d) consumer charging, billing, collection and credit practices; 49 (e) non-payment of bills, disconnections and re-connections; (f) compensating electricity consumers who do not enjoy the contracted electricity services; (g) the establishment of a forum at which electricity consumers are able to express their views and raise concerns and procedures for addressing those concerns; (h) fault repairs and response to emergencies; (i) the rights and duties of electricity consumers and available remedies; (j) the protection of consumer data; and (k) the provision and dissemination of information. (2) The consumer service standards, practices and procedures developed by the Commission and any amendments shall be published on the website of the Commission. (3) Without prejudice to the provisions of subsection (1) of this section , the Commission may require licensees to prepare , review or amend individual consumer standards, practices or procedures in relation to specific matters for their respective co nsumers and such standards, practices or procedures shall be subject to the prior approval of and ratification by the Commission and published by the licensee on its website. (4) The Commission shall collaborate with the Plateau State Consumer Protection Agency in connection with the matters set out in this section. PART XVI EMISSIONS CONTROL, RENEWABLE ENERGY, ENERGY EFFICIENCY, AND DEMAND SIDE MANAGEMENT

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 80. Functions of the Commission under this Part The functions of the Commission unde
chunks.text: 80. Functions of the Commission under this Part The functions of the Commission under this Part are to: (a) promote the use of renewable energy sources for electricity generation; (b) promote energy efficiency and demand side management practices; (c) promote the transition from utilization of distillates as fuel for electricity generation at all levels in the State to gas or renewable energy sources; (d) ensure minimal adverse environmental impact to th e State from electricity generating plants and other electricity facilities, networks, equipment, infrastructure; and (e) address the significant amount of environmentally damaging emissions from electricity generating plants in the State.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 81. General Responsibility of the Plateau State Government 50 (1) The Plateau State
chunks.text: 81. General Responsibility of the Plateau State Government 50 (1) The Plateau State Government shall take steps to: (a) support, promote, create an enabling investment environment and introduce measures, strategies, incentives, schemes and programmes to increase and foster the utilization of gas and renewable energy sources for generation of electricity in the State, and the implementation of energy efficiency and demand side management practices; (b) ensure that the State fulfils an exemplary role having regard to the objectives of this Law, including by: (i) requiring that buildings owned or occupied by the State or its agencies and bodies utilize renewable energy sources for electricity generation , and implement energy efficiency and demand side management practices; (ii) allowing infrastructure owned or occupied by the State or its agencies to be used by third parties for installations that produce electricity from renewable energy sources; (iii) ensuring that State agencies and bodies carry out energy audits and implement the recommendations of the audits; (iv) ensuring the utilization of energy-efficient products by State agencies and bodies ; and (v) ensuring that building and construction codes in the State are modified to foster the adoption of energy efficient standards; (c) facilitate research and development activities in relation to renewable energy, energy efficiency and demand side management; and (d) ensure relevant cooperation and collaboration with the Federal Government and such other agency, body, or ent ity, including any international organisation in furtherance of the objectives of this Law. (2) The Ministry shall be the coordinating body for incentives, strategies, schemes and programmes introduced by the State pursuant to subsection 1 of this section, provided that the Governor may designate any other ministry, body, agency or entity as the coordinating body in relation to any specific incentive, strategy, scheme or programme.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 82. Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan (1) The Min
chunks.text: 82. Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan (1) The Ministry shall, in consultation with relevant stakeholders: (a) within eighteen (18) months of the commencement of this Law or such other extended period as may be approved by the Governor, develop a Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan for the State; and (b) review, amend or modify the Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan from time to time but at least every five (5) years from the development of the first edition of the Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan. 51 (2) The Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan and any revision, amendment or modification shall be subject to the approval of the State Executive Council and shall be published on the website of the Ministry. (3) The Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan shall as a minimum provide for the following matters: (a) the State’s short, medium and long term renewable energy, energy efficiency and demand side management targets and incentives; (b) the role of the State in incentivizing and creating an enabling environment to encourage utilization of renewable energy sources for generation of electricity , and promoting energy efficiency and demand side management measures; (c) programmes to encourage the utilization of renewable energy sources for generation of electricity and adoption of energy efficiency and demand side management practices; (d) the role of key stakeholders in the implementation of the strategy and action plan; (e) a process to periodically identify the gaps between current and target levels, develop action plans aimed at closing or addressing the identified gaps; (f) priority activities to be implemented annually by the State; (g) a monitoring system for data collection and impact tracking , including assigning responsibility for the specification, collection, storage, maintenance and supply of relevant data on renewable energy utilization, energy efficiency and demand side management measures and practices; and (h) annual reviews, audits and reporting of re

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 83. Promotion of Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and Demand Side Management (1)
chunks.text: 83. Promotion of Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and Demand Side Management (1) The Commission shall: (a) implement the Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and DSM Strategy and Action Plan; (b) design and introduce adequate measures to drive the adoption of renewable energy sources by licensees, market participants and electricity consumers; and (c) encourage energy efficiency and demand side management practices. (2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1) of this section, the Commission may design and introduce any of the measures set out below to promote the adoption of renewable energy sources for electricity generation and encourage energy efficiency and demand side management practices: (a) provide streamlined, simplified and expedite d administrative, authorization and permitting procedures; (b) coordinate with other authorities and bodies to accelerate permitting requirements; 52 (c) ensure that administrative charges paid or payable are transparent and cost-related; (d) ensure long-term, stable and favourable tariff methodology for electricity generated from renewable energy sources; (e) subject to requirements relating to the maintenance of the safety, reliability and efficiency of the State electricity system and based on clearly defined transparent and non-discriminatory criteria: (i) guarantee the transmission or distribution of electricity generated from renewable energy sources; (ii) provide for priority a ccess or guaranteed access to the State grid of electricity generated from renewable energy sources; (iii) ensure that in the dispatch of electricity generated, priority is given to electricity generated using renewable energy sources; (f) ensure the development of transparent and non-discriminatory rules for the connection of a generator of electricity from a renewable energy source to the State grid; (g) mechanism for the issuance of guarantees of origin in response to a request from a producer of electricity from renewable energy sources within the State; (h) require and incentivize electricity consumers or any class thereof to carry out energy audit and implement the recommendations from the audits; (i) introduce certification

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 84. Emissions Standards, Permit, Fee, Etc
chunks.text: 84. Emissions Standards, Permit, Fee, Etc. (1) The Commission shall issue regulations: (a) prescribing mandatory emissions standards and limits in respect of the use of distillates for electricity generation; (b) addressing any matter as may be relevant to the environmentally friendly operation of the Plateau State Electricity Market; and (c) provide for such other matters as the Commission may consider necessary. (2) The Commission may by regulations: (a) require that electricity generating plants or any class thereof located and utilised for any purpose in the State employing distillates as fuel to transit to gas or renewable energy sources within a transition period, which period shall not be less than six (6) months or more than twenty-four (24) months from the effective date of the regulation; (b) mandate electricity generating plants or any class thereof located and utilised in the State with an emission level above the prescribed emission standards to apply for a permit from the Commission, subject to such terms and conditions as the Commission may specify; (c) require the payment into the Electrification Fund of an emissions levy by each individual electricity generating plant located and utilised in the State with an emission level above the prescribed emission standards; (d) provide for the method of calculating the amount of emissions fee payable and the procedure for collection; and (e) introduce such disincentives as it may consider necessary to ensure the utilization of the cleanest available fuel for electricity generation. (3) The proceeds of all emissions levies shall be paid into the Electrification Fund. (4) The Commission shall make arrangements for monitoring compliance with the regulations made pursuant to subsections (1) and (2) of this section. (5) The Commission shall co llaborate with the Plateau State Environmental Protection Agency in connection with the matters set out in this section.
