chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 85. General Responsibilities of the Plateau State Government in connection with Off-
chunks.text: 85. General Responsibilities of the Plateau State Government in connection with Off-Grid Solutions (1) The Plateau State Government shall take steps to: (a) support, promote, create an enabling investment environment and introduce measures, strategies, incentives, schemes and programmes for the deployment of off-grid solutions in the State; and (b) ensure relevant cooperation and collaboration with the Federal Government and such other agency, body, or entity, including any international organisation in furtherance of the objectives of this Law. (2) The Ministry shall be the coordinating body for incentives, strategies, schemes and programmes introduced by the State pursuant to subsection (1) of this section: Provided that the Governor may designate any other ministry, body, agency or entity as the coordinating body in relation to any specific incentive, strategy, scheme or programme.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 86. The Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan (1) The Ministry shall, in
chunks.text: 86. The Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan (1) The Ministry shall, in consultation with relevant stakeholders: (a) within six (6) months of the commencement of this Law or such extended period as may be approved by the Governor , e stablish and publish relevant criteria for identifying, and accordingly identify, all unserved and underserved areas, communities and clusters in the State; (b) within eighteen (18) months from the commencement of this Law or such extended period as may be approved by the Governor, develop an Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan for the State; and (c) review, amend or modify the Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan from time to time but at least every three (3) years from the development of the first edition of the Off - Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan. (2) The Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan and any revision, amendment or modification shall be subject to the approval of the State Executive Council and shall be published on the website of the Agency. (3) The Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan shall as a minimum provide for the following: (a) recognition of off -grid solutions as a vital component of the Plateau Integrated Resource Plan; (b) the State’s short, medium and long term targets for off-grid solutions; (c) map potential cost effective off-grid solutions suitable to each unserved or underserved area, community or cluster in the State and the nature of incentives that may be provided to such locations and to licensees to drive the provision of off-grid solutions; (d) the role of the State in incentivizing and providing the enabling en vironment to catalyze private sector investment in creating an ecosystem for off-grid solutions in the State; 55 (e) a basis for developing education, research, sensitization, consumer protection, and capacity building programmes for off-grid solutions in the State; (f) regulatory principles applicable to off-grid solutions and e-waste in the State; (g) strategies for the promotion of gender and social inclusion in driving electricity access; (h) programmes, projects and activities to be implemented to drive of

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 87. Establishment of the Plateau State Electrification Agency (1) There is establish
chunks.text: 87. Establishment of the Plateau State Electrification Agency (1) There is established the Plateau State Electrification Agency (referred to in this Law as “the Agency”), which shall replace the Plateau State Electricity Board. (2) The Agency shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal and shall in its corporate name be capable of: (a) suing and being sued; (b) acquiring, owning, holding, mortgaging, developing, disposing and otherwise dealing howsoever with property, whether movable or immovable, subject to the extant policies of the State; (c) entering into contracts, subject to the extant policies of the State; and (d) doing or performing all other things or acts for the furtherance of its functions and duties under this Law which may be lawfully done or performed by a body corporate. (3) The Agency shall be under the supervision of the Honourable Commissioner.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 88. Functions of the Agency (1) The Agency shall: (a) control and manage any electri
chunks.text: 88. Functions of the Agency (1) The Agency shall: (a) control and manage any electricity installation vested in the Agency under the provisions of this Law or any other law; (b) construct, reconstruct, maintain and operate public lighting or power points in any street or other public place; (c) construct, reconstruct, maintain and operate electric ity installations, works, buildings , infrastructure and other works necessary for the discharge of its functions; 56 (d) carry any electricity installation through, across, over or under any street or any place laid out or intended as a street after giving reasonable notice in writing to the affected owner or occupier, and make good any damage done; (e) enter any land at any time between the hours of 6.00am and 6.00pm after giving reasonable notice in writing to the affected owner or occupier for the purpose of electricity installations, examining, repairing or removing any electricity installation which is the property of the Agency; and (f) perform such other functions and exercise such powers that are necessary and incidental to the above. (2) In addition to subsection (1) of this section, the Agency shall also carry out the following functions: (a) promote the deployment of environmentally friendly and climate-efficient electricity solutions in the underserved and unserved areas of the State; (b) increase access to electricity services for underserved and unserved areas of the State , including through engaging with and facilitating entities wishing to supply such services; (c) be responsible for executing and implementing the Off -Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan; (d) manage and supervise the Electrification Fund in accordance with the provisions of this Law and any approved operational guidelines, procedures, criteria and/or modalities; (e) collaborate generally with relevant ministries, departments and agencies of the State and Federal Government to facilitate the electrification of underserved and unserved areas of the State and the general provision of off-grid solutions; (f) promote capacity building in relation to the provision of off-grid solutions; (g) create public awareness through seminars

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 89. Consultation by the Agency In discharging its functions under this Law, the Agen
chunks.text: 89. Consultation by the Agency In discharging its functions under this Law, the Agency shall consult such persons, groups or associations who may be affected by its activities, programmes or projects. 90. Relationship with the Commission 57 Nothing in this Law shall be construed as conferring the Agency with powers to exercise regulatory functions over any aspect of the Plateau State Electricity Market, or interfere with the functions, duties and powers of the Commission: Provided that the Commission shall consult the Agency in the making of any regulations in relation to the functions and powers of the Agency under this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 91. Establishment and Composition of the Board of the Agency (1) There is establishe
chunks.text: 91. Establishment and Composition of the Board of the Agency (1) There is established for the Agency a governing board (referred to in this Law as “the Board of the Agency”) which shall perform the functions of the Agency as stipulated under this Part. (2) The Board of the Agency shall consist of five (5) Directors, made up of: (a) a non-executive Chairperson; (b) the Managing Director of the Agency; (c) a representative of the Ministry nominated by the Honourable Commissioner, who shall be a non-executive Director; and (d) two (2) part-time non-executive Directors. (3) A Director shall stand in a fiduciary relationship towards the Agency and shall observe utmost good faith towards the Agency in the exercise of his powers and discharge of his functions. (4) The Agency shall however not be incapacitated from carrying out its functions and exercising its powers by virtue of any vacancy in the composition of the Board of the Agency or defect in the appointment of any Director.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 92. Powers of the Board of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall: (a) provide
chunks.text: 92. Powers of the Board of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall: (a) provide general guidance for the carrying out of the functions of the Agency; (b) review and approve the annual budget, operating, business and strategic plans of the Agency; (c) be responsible for devising means of generating independent revenue through contributions, grants, donations and gifts for the Electrification Fund as it may deem fit in accordance with this Law; (d) supervise and ensure accountability in relation to the Electrification Fund established under this Law; (e) develop relevant operational guidelines , procedures, criteria and/or modalities for the allocation, management and utilization of the Electrification Fund; 58 (f) prepare the annual plan setting out the proposed activities, programmes and projects with their cost implications to be funded with the sums of money accruing to the Electrification Fund; (g) structure the Agency into such number of departments as it deems fit for the effective discharge of the functions of the Agency, subject to the approval of the Honourable Commissioner; and (h) exercise such other powers as may be necessary for the efficient and effective administration of the Agency under this Law. (2) The Honourable Commissioner may give the Board of the Agency such general directives in relation to the discharge of its functions and the exercise of its powers under this Law as may appear to be necessary to ensure conformity by the Board of the Agency with the policy of the Government and the Board of the Agency shall give effect to such directives.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 93. Appointment of the Chairperson and the Non-Executive Directors (1) The Chairpers
chunks.text: 93. Appointment of the Chairperson and the Non-Executive Directors (1) The Chairperson and other non-executive Directors of the Board of the Agency excluding the ex - officio member shall be persons of proven integrity and ability and shall be appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Honourable Commissioner. (2) The Chairperson and other non -executive Directors of the Board of the Agency excluding the ex- officio member shall be persons with relevant professional qualifications and cognate experience in the fields of energy, procurement, engineering, law or other relevant disciplines and must have senior management experience either in the public or private sector. (3) The Chairperson and the non-executive Directors shall hold office on part-time basis for a period of four (4) years and shall be eligible for reappointment for one (1) further term of four (4) years only.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 94. Managing Director of the Agency (1) The Managing Director shall be appointed by
chunks.text: 94. Managing Director of the Agency (1) The Managing Director shall be appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Honourable Commissioner. (2) A person shall be qualified for appointment as the Managing Director if such person: (a) is a holder of a university degree recognized in Nigeria in the fields of law, accountancy, economics, finance, administration, energy or engineering; (b) has not less than fifteen (15) years working experience in the relevant field, seven (7) of which is at a senior management level; and (c) has extensive managerial, technical or professional knowledge of and experience in connection with the power sector. (3) The Managing Director shall be: 59 (a) appointed for an initial term of f our (4) years and shall be eligible, su bject to satisfactory performance, for reappointment for one (1) further term of four (4) years only; (b) the chief executive and accounting officer of the Agency; and (c) responsible to the Board of the Agency for the day-to-day administration of the Agency. (4) Except as provided in this Law, the terms and conditions of appointment of the Managing Director shall be specified in his letter of appointment. (5) The Managing Director shall devote his full time to the service of the Agency and while holding office shall not hold any other office or employment except where appointed by virtue of his office into the membership of any board, agency or authority of the government of the State or any organization to which the Agency is a member or an affiliate.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 95. Secretary of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall appoint a secretary an
chunks.text: 95. Secretary of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall appoint a secretary and legal adviser (referred to in this Law as “the Secretary of the Agency ”) who shall be a legal practitioner qualified to practice in Nigeria, with at least ten (10) years post-call experience. (2) The Secretary of the Agency shall: (a) be the head of the legal department; (b) act as the legal adviser to the Agency; (c) arrange and attend meetings of the Board of the Agency and keep minutes, corporate records and the common seal of the Agency; and (d) discharge such other administrative and other secretarial duties as the Managing Director or the Board of the Agency may assign.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 96. Other Staff of the Agency (1) The Agency may employ such other staff as it may d
chunks.text: 96. Other Staff of the Agency (1) The Agency may employ such other staff as it may deem necessary to assist the Agency in the performance of its functions under this Law. (2) The terms and conditions of service, including remuneration, allowances and other benefits of the staff of the Agency and the periodic review of the same, shall be as determined by the Board of the Agency having regard to the extant financial policies and guidelines of the State. (3) The Agency may, subject to the provisions of this Law, make staff regulations, rules and policies relating generally to the conditions of service of the staff of the Agency. (4) The Agency may assign to its staff such functions of the Agency as the Agency deems fit. (5) The provisions of the Pension Reform Law shall be applicable to the officers, staff or employees of the Agency. 60 (6) Nothing in subsection (5) of this section shall prevent the Agency from appointing a person to an office on terms that preclude the grant of pension or other retirement benefits in respect of that office.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 97. Cessation of Office of Members of the Board of the Agency (1) A member of the Bo
chunks.text: 97. Cessation of Office of Members of the Board of the Agency (1) A member of the Board of the Agency shall cease to hold office if the member: (a) resigns by giving three (3) months written notice to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner, upon expiration of the said period of time; (b) is unfit or unable to discharge the functions of the office whether by reason of infirmity or mental incapacity; (c) has been convicted for offences involving dishonesty; (d) is an undischarged bankrupt; (e) ceases to be an official of the Ministry, in the case of the ex-officio non-executive Director; (f) has demonstrated an inability to effectively carry out the functions of his/her office; or (g) is guilty of a serious misconduct in relation to his/her duties and performance of his functions as a member of the Board of the Agency. (2) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1), the Governor may remove any membe r of the Board of the Agency, if satisfied that it is in the public interest to do so. (3) Any vacancy in the Board of the Agency shall be filled by the Governor.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 98. Remuneration and Allowances (1) The non-executive Directors, other than the ex -
chunks.text: 98. Remuneration and Allowances (1) The non-executive Directors, other than the ex -officio member shall be paid such remuneration , allowances and other benefits as the Governor may approve. (2) The remuneration, allowances and other benefits of the Managing Director shall be as specified in his letter of appointment as approved by the Governor. (3) The remuneration, allowances and other benefits of the Directors referred to in subsections (1) and (2) shall be paid from the funds of the Agency subject to the extant financial policies and guidelines of the State. 99. Code of Ethics for the Agency The Board of th e Agency shall develop and issue a comprehensive code of ethics which shall apply to all Directors and staff of the Agency.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 100. Proceedings of the Board of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall meet no
chunks.text: 100. Proceedings of the Board of the Agency (1) The Board of the Agency shall meet not more than four (4) times in every financial year except in case of emergencies. 61 (2) The Chairperson may summon an emergency meeting of the Board of the Agency, but shall at any time call an emergency meeting upon a written request by a majority of the members of the Board of the Agency. (3) The Chairperson shall preside at every meeting of the Board of the Agency and in the absence of the Chairperson, one of the members except the Managing Director shall be appointed to preside. (4) Unless otherwise agreed by all the members of the Board of the Agency, at least five (5) days written notice of every meeting of the Board of the Agency shall be given to every member of the Board of the Agency. (5) Any question for decision before the Board of the Agency shall be decided by the majority of votes of members present and voting and where there is an equality of votes, the Chair person presiding shall have a deliberative and casting vote. (6) The quorum of any meeting of the Board of the Agency shall be four (4) members but in the event of an election, the person who chairs the meeting shall not vote. (7) Where the Board of the Agency desires to obtain the advice of any person on a matter, the Board of the Agency may co-opt the person as a member for such period as it thinks fit, provided that a person co-opted shall not be entitled to vote at any meeting of the Board of the Agency and shall not count towards a quorum.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 101. Common Seal of the Agency The common seal of the Agency shall be determined by t
chunks.text: 101. Common Seal of the Agency The common seal of the Agency shall be determined by the Board of the Agency and the affixing of the common seal shall be authenticated by the signatures of the Managing Director and the Secretary , or any other member authorized by the Board of the Agency to act for that purpose. 102. Funds of the Agency (1) The Agency shall establish and maintain a fund (referred to in this Law as “the Fund of the Agency”). (2) There shall be paid and credited into the Fund of the Agency: (a) such sums of money as may be appropriated to the Agency in annual budgetary allocations; (b) all fees earned by the Agency for any service provided by the Agency in the exercise of its functions under this Law; (c) all sums of money accruing to the Agency by way of grants -in-aids, gifts, testamentary dispositions, endowments and contributions from any other source provided that the condition for such grant s is not in consistent with the objectives, functions, duties and responsibilities of the Agency under this Law; (d) any other fund that may be created from time to time by a Law of the House; and (e) all other monetary assets that may from time to time accrue to the Agency. 62 (3) The Agency shall manage its funds in accordance with the extant financial policies and guidelines of the State. 103. Power of the Agency to Borrow The Board of the Agency may with the approval of the Governor and the House borrow such sums of money for and in connection with the performance of its functions under this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 104. Financial Provisions (1) The Agency shall, not later than 30th September in each
chunks.text: 104. Financial Provisions (1) The Agency shall, not later than 30th September in each financial year, prepare and present to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner for approval, a budget showing the estimated income and expenditure for the following financial year. (2) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1) of this section, the Agency may also, in any financial year, prepare and present to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner for approval, supplementary or adjusted statements of estimated income and expenditure. (3) Subject to subsections (1) and (2) of this section, the Agency shall apply the Fund of the Agency: (a) to meet the administrative and operating costs of the Agency; (b) for the payment of salaries, fees, remuneration, allowances, pensions and other retirement benefits payable to the Directors and the staff of the Agency, as the case may be; (c) for the purchase or acquisition of property, equipment and other capital expenditure and for maintenance of any property acquired or vested in the Agency; and (d) for or in connection with all or any of the functions of the Agency under this Law or any applicable regulations.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 105. Establishment of the Plateau State Electrification Fund (1) There is established
chunks.text: 105. Establishment of the Plateau State Electrification Fund (1) There is established the Plateau State Electrification Fund (referred to in this Law as the “Electrification Fund”) and it shall be controlled, operated and managed by the Agency in the manner specified in this Part. (2) The Electrification Fund shall comprise funds derived from but not limited to the following sources: (a) such sums of money as may be appropriated to the Electrification Fund in annual budgetary allocation; (b) a percentage as approved by the Governor of any excess of the Commission’s revenue of any year over the approved expenditure for that year; (c) all fines and penalties imposed and collected by the Commission in enforcing any provisions of this Law or regulations made by the Commission, which shall be paid directly into the Electrification Fund within fifteen (15) days of collection; 63 (d) any electricity levy introduced by the Commission pursuant to this Law; (e) donations, contributions, gifts, loans, grants, aids and such other assets that may from time to time specifically accrue to the Electrification Fund; (f) earnings, interest and other income accruing from the investments made and project funded with such money accruing to the Electrification Fund and the principal sum invested upon maturation; and (g) any special intervention fund as may be provided by the State. (3) The Board of the Agency shall ensure that the Electrification Fund is at all times transparently managed and operated and totally separated from the Fund of the Agency. (4) The Commission shall ensure that all such money payable by the Commission into the Electrification Fund are paid promptly and directly into the Electrification Fund. (5) Any money, grants, donations, contributions or the like given to the Electrification Fund in any foreign currency shall be held by the Agency as part of the Electrification Fund but until they are to be utilized, such funds shall be held in the currency in which they were given to the Electrification Fund and be accounted for accordingly. (6) The assets and mon ey in the Electrification Fund shall not be used in any manner whatsoever to defray or undertake the recur

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 106. Utilization of the Electrification Fund (1) The Board of the Agency shall at the
chunks.text: 106. Utilization of the Electrification Fund (1) The Board of the Agency shall at the beginning of every financial year but no later than February, prepare an annual plan setting out the proposed activities, programmes and projects with their cost implications to be funded with the mone y accruing to the Electrification Fund for approval by the Honourable Commissioner. (2) The Electrification Fund shall only be utilized for the following purposes, to: (a) implement the Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan; (b) promote, support and provide electricity access and services to underserved and unserved areas of the State; (c) promote and support the expansion of the State grid, and the development, deployment and utilization of off-grid solutions in the State; (d) subject to the financial regulations of the State, make investments as may be approved by the Board of the Agency provided that such investments shall not undermine the ability of the Agency to meet its obligations; and (e) pay for the costs and expenses in re lation to the administration and operation of the Electrification Fund: Provided such costs and expenses do not exceed in any financial year 64 zero point seventy -five percent (0.75%) of the amounts standing to the credit of the Electrification Fund at the end of the previous financial year. (3) The Board of the Agency shall, in consultation with the Honourable Commi ssioner and other stakeholders: (a) develop and establish objective and transparent guidelines, criteria and/or modalities for the management, allocation and utilization of proceeds from the Electrification Fund; and (b) develop and establish open, competitive and transparent procedure s for screening and selecting eligible activities, programmes and projects to receive disbursements from the Electrification Fund.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 107. Special Purpose Funds (1) The Board of the Agency may, subject to the prior appr
chunks.text: 107. Special Purpose Funds (1) The Board of the Agency may, subject to the prior approval of the Governor, execute agreements with development partners setting up special purpose funds for the provision of off-grid solutions in any part of the State. (2) The agreements made pursuant to subsection (1) may set out separate financing arrangements in respect of the management and utilization of the special purpose funds and clearly establish the modalities for administering the special purpose funds, provided that in the absence of such defined financing arrangement or administrative modalities, the rules, procedures and guidelines applicable to the Electrification Fund established under this Law shall apply to such special purpose funds. 108. Restriction on Execution against Money in the Electrification Fund No execution or attachment process shall be issued against any money standing to the credit of the Electrification Fund or accruing to the Electrification Fund. 109. Maintenance of Proper Accounts and Records The Agency shall, in respect of each year, keep proper accounts and other records relating to such accounts in respect of all of the Agency’s activities, operations, transactions, funds (including the Electrification Fund), properties and such other accounts and records as the Honourable Commissioner may require.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 110. Audit of the Accounts and Records of the Agency (1) The Agency shall ensure that
chunks.text: 110. Audit of the Accounts and Records of the Agency (1) The Agency shall ensure that its accounts and other records kept shall be audited within three (3) months from the end of each financial year by auditors whose appointment s shall be approved by the Board of the Agency provided that such auditors are on the list of auditors approved from time to time by the Auditor-General of the State. (2) The Auditor shall be entitled to require to be produced all accounts and other records relating to each account which are kept by the Agency or its Directors, Members, Staff, Agents, Consultants or Service Providers and to require from any Director, Member, Staff, Agent, Consultant or Service Provider of the Agency such information as in the Auditor’s opinion are necessary for the purposes of the audit. 111. Reports of the Agency 65 (1) The Agency shall prepare and submit to the Governor through the Honourable Commissioner annually, and to the House not later than four (4) months after the end of its financial year, a report on the activities and operations of the Agency for the preceding financial year and shall include the Agency’s audited accounts for the year under review together with the Auditor’s Report. (2) The Agency’s Report under subsection (1) of this section shall include a progress report with details of the implementation of the Off-Grid Electrification Strategy and Action Plan by the Agency and the utilization of the Electrification Fund. (3) The Agency shall publish the Report submitted on its website.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 112. Restriction on Execution on the Agency’s Installation An execution and attachmen
chunks.text: 112. Restriction on Execution on the Agency’s Installation An execution and attachment of process shall not be issued against any electrical installation vested in or being the property of the Agency. PART XVIII POWER ENFORCEMENT UNIT AND CRIMINAL PROVISIONS 113. Establishment of the Power Enforcement Unit (1) For the purposes of this Law, there shall be constituted by the Honourable Commissioner an ad-hoc enforcement unit in the Ministry (referred to in this Law as “the Power Enforcement Unit”) which shall consist of: (a) a Chairperson who shall be an officer in the Ministry not below grade level 15; (b) officials of the Ministry as may be assigned to the Power Enforcement Unit; (c) a legal practitioner from the Ministry of Justice of the State as may be assigned to the Power Enforcement Unit; (d) law enforcement agents as may be deployed or assigned to the Power Enforcement Unit; (e) two (2) representatives of licensees, market participants or other stakeholders, one (1) of which must be from a distribution licensee; and (f) other persons as may be required by the Power Enforcement Unit for the purpose of carrying out the functions and exercising the powers of the Power Enforcement Unit under this Law. (2) The power of arrest shall be vested in the Power Enforcement Unit and any other Law Enforcement Unit/Agency in the State.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 114. Functions of the Power Enforcement Unit The functions of Power Enforcement Unit
chunks.text: 114. Functions of the Power Enforcement Unit The functions of Power Enforcement Unit shall include: (a) liaising with the Ministry of Justice of the State in connection with the prosecution of offences created under the provisions of this Law or any applicable regulations; 66 (b) liaising with the Commission, licensees, market participants and other stakeholders to address issues of electricity theft, theft of and damage to electricity installations and infrastructure and other connected matters; (c) liaising with the Commission in connection with the whistle blowing scheme created pursuant to this Law; and (d) carrying out such other activities as are necessary to prevent the commission of the offences created under this law or any applicable law/regulations.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 115. Powers of the Power Enforcement Unit (1) A duly authorized officer of the Power
chunks.text: 115. Powers of the Power Enforcement Unit (1) A duly authorized officer of the Power Enforcement Unit shall have the power to: (a) enter upon any premises at which any undertaking is carried out without licence as required under this law or any applicable law/regulations, or an offence under this Law or any applicable regulations is or is suspected to have been committed , at any time between the hours of 6.00am and 6.00pm or in the case of an emergency, at any other time; (b) inspect and test any process, installation, works or other operation which is o r appears to be carried out in those premises; (c) enter, inspect, and search any place or premises in which such officer has reason to believe that electricity has been, is being or is likely to be used unlawfully, provided that such search shall be limited to the meter and related surroundings and devices; (d) search, seize and remove all such devices, instruments, wires and any other facilitator or article which have been or are being, utilized for the unauthorized use of electricity; (e) examine or seize any books of account or documents which in his opinion shall be useful for or relevant to, any proceedings in respect of the offence of theft of electricity and allow the person from whose custody such books of account or documents are seized to make copies thereof or take extracts in the presence of the officer; (f) enter, inspect, any place or premises into which electricity service has been provided or into which electrical works is supplied, at any time between the hours of 6.00am and 6.00pm or in the case of an emergency, at any other time, so as to: (i) ascertain the amount of electricity taken or used; or (ii) disconnect the supply of electricity to any occupier, or to diminish or withhold the supply of electricity to any household through or by means of any service, either wholly or in part for the purpose of carrying out maintenance or where the consumer defaults in paying for the electricity consumed; (g) inspect any service to ascertain whether there is any obstruction or damage to any service or meter and anything in connection with it; and (h) inspect and ensure that electricity has been, is be

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 116. Theft of Electricity (1) Any person who: (a) willfully and unlawfully taps, make
chunks.text: 116. Theft of Electricity (1) Any person who: (a) willfully and unlawfully taps, makes or causes to be made any connection with overhead, underground or underwater lines or cables, or service wires, or service facilities or by any other means whatsoever, of a licensee or supplier, as the case may be; (b) without lawful right (the proof of which shall be upon him) abstracts, branches off or diverts or causes to be abstracted, branched off or diverted any electrical energy, or consumes or uses any such electrical energy which has been wrongfully or unlawfully abstracted, branched off or diverted, knowing it to have been wrongfully or unlawfully abstracted, branched off or diverted; (c) disconnects, or permits to be disconnected, any conductor or apparatus from any electric supply line belonging to a licensee, without the consent of the licensee; (d) makes or permits to be made any alteration in his /her permanent installation without the prior approval of the licensee; (e) willfully and unlawfully tampers with a meter, installs or uses a tampered meter, current reversing transformer, loop connection or any other device or method which interferes with accurate or proper registration, calibration o r metering of electric al energy or otherwise results in a manner whereby electricity is stolen or wasted; (f) in any case where the quantity of the supply of electricity is not ascertained by a meter, uses any apparatus or device other than what he /she has contracted to pay for or uses such apparatus or device at any other time than the tim e specified and for which he /she has contracted to pay; (g) supplies any other person with any part of the electricity supplied to him/her by the licensee, without the consent of the licensee; (h) uses or receive the direct benefit of electric ity obtained through any of the acts mentioned above; or (i) uses electricity for the purpose other than which the usage of electricity was authorized; commits an offence under this Law and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine of at least three (3) times the value of the quantity of the electricity used, wasted or stolen for an individual or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one (1

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 117. Restoration of Supply Without Consent Any person, who without the consent of the
chunks.text: 117. Restoration of Supply Without Consent Any person, who without the consent of the licensee, restores a supply of electricity to any premises where such supply has been discontinued by the licensee in the exercise of its rights commits an offence under this Law and shall, on conviction, be liabl e to a fine of at least three (3) times the value of the quantity of the electricity used, wasted or stolen for an individual or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one (1) year, or to both such fine and imprisonment, and in case of a continuing event , a daily fine not exceeding Five Thousand Naira (N5,000.00) and in the case of a body corporate, it shall be liable to a fine of at least six (6) times the value of the quantity of the electricity used, wasted or stolen and in case of a continuing event, a daily fine not exceeding Ten Thousand Naira (N10,000.00).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 118. Theft of Electric Lines and Materials A person who willfully and unlawfully: (a)
chunks.text: 118. Theft of Electric Lines and Materials A person who willfully and unlawfully: (a) cuts or removes or takes away or transfers any electric line, material or meter f rom a tower, pole, any other installation or place of installation or any other place, or site where it may be rightfully or lawfully stored, deposited, kept, stocked, situated, or located, including during transportation, without the consent of the licensee or the owner, as the case may be, whether or not the act is done for profit or gain; (b) stores, possesses, or otherwise keeps in his /her premises, custody or control, any electric line, material or meter without the consent of the licensee or owner, whether or not the act is committed for profit or gain; or (c) loads, carries, or moves from one place to another any electric line, material or meter without the consent of the licensee or its owner, whether or not the act is done for profit or gain; commits an offence under this Law and shall, in addition to other punishments as may be prescribed under any other law for such acts, be liable on conviction to a fine of at least five (5) times the value of any of the items taken or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three (3) years , or to both such fine and imprisonment.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 119. Damaging Infrastructure (1) A person who willfully or unlawfully: (a) destroys,
chunks.text: 119. Damaging Infrastructure (1) A person who willfully or unlawfully: (a) destroys, damages or removes any infrastructure, material, installation, equipment, or infrastructure connected with the supply of electricity; or 69 (b) destroys, damages or removes any electricity transmission or distribution line; commits an offence under this Law and shall be liable on conviction to a fine of at least five (5) times the value of replacement of any such infras tructure, material, installation, equipment or electricity transmission or distribution line destroyed, damaged or removed including costs of replacement or repair or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three (3) years, or to both such fine and imprisonment. (2) A person who willfully or unlawfully: (a) prevents or obstructs the delivery of electricity through any act; or (b) prevents or obstructs the transmission or distribution of electricity; commits an offence under this Law and shall be liable on conviction to imprisonment for a term not less than six (6) months, or to a fine not less than Five Hundred Thousand Naira (N500,000.00), or to both such fine and imprisonment, and in case of a continuing event, a daily fine not less than Five Thousand Naira (N5,000.00).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 120. Hindering, Obstructing or Interfering with the Exercise of Licensee Powers (1) A
chunks.text: 120. Hindering, Obstructing or Interfering with the Exercise of Licensee Powers (1) A person who willfully or unlawfully obstructs, restrains, prevents, harasses, injures or otherwise interferes with any person lawfully carrying on duties of generation, transmission, system operation, distribution, trading or supply of electricity commits an offence under this Law. (2) A person hindering, obstructing or interfering with the exercise by a licensee with regard to an electric supply line, or by the servants or agents duly authorized in writing of any such licensee, of any right of entry upon land for the purpose of laying and connecting, or repairing, inspecting or removing, an electric supply line commits an offence under this Law. (3) A person who impersonates or falsely presents or parades as an employee of a licen see commits an offence under this Law. (4) Any person that commits an offence pursuant to this section shall on conviction be liable to a fine not less than Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira (N250,000.00), or to imprisonment for a term not less than six (6) months, or to both such fine and imprisonment.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 121. Evidence of Illegal Use of Electricity Any of the following circumstances shall
chunks.text: 121. Evidence of Illegal Use of Electricity Any of the following circumstances shall constitute prima facie evidence of illegal use of electricity by the beneficiary of such use: (a) presence of a drilled hole on the cover of the meter or at the back or any part of said meter; (b) presence of any elements inside the meter that could result in t he inaccurate registration of the meter’s internal parts to prevent its accurate registration of consumption of electricity; (c) existence of any wiring connection which affects the normal operation or registration of the meter; 70 (d) the presence of a tampered, broken or fake seal on the meter or mutilated, altered or tampered meter recording chart or graph or computerized chart, graph or log; (e) presence of a current reversing transformer, jumper, shorting and/or shunting wire and/or loop connection or any other similar device in any part of a building or its premises which is subject to the control of the consumer or on the meter; (f) mutilation, alteration, reconnection , disconnection, bypassing or tampering of instruments, transformers, and accessories; (g) destruction of, or attempt to destroy any integral accessory of the metering devise box which encases a meter or its metering accessories; or (h) acceptance of money and/or other valuable consideration by any officer or employee of the electric utility concerned or the making of such an offer to any such officer or employee for not reporting the presence of any of the circumstances enumerated in this section.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 122. Evidence of Theft of Transmission or Distribution Lines and Materials The posses
chunks.text: 122. Evidence of Theft of Transmission or Distribution Lines and Materials The possession, control or custody of transmission or distribution lines or materials by any person, natural or legal entity, not engaged in the generation, transmission or distribution of electricity, or in the manufacture of such transmission or distribution lines or materials shall be prima facie evidence of theft of transmission or distribution lines and materials, and such line s or material may be confiscated from the person in possession, control or custody of the same.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 123. Offences by Incorporated Entities (1) Where an offence under this Law or any reg
chunks.text: 123. Offences by Incorporated Entities (1) Where an offence under this Law or any regulations made pursuant to this Law has been committed by a legal entity or other corporate vehicle, company, firm, corporation or association, every person who at the time the offence was committed was a Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Director, Manager, Secretary or other similar officer of the entity or was purporting to act in any such capacity or was in any manner or to any extent responsible for the management of any of the affairs of the body corporate or was assisting in such management: (a) may be charged severally or jointly in the same proceedings with the entity; and (b) if the entity is found guilty of the offence, shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence. (2) Nothing contained in subsection (1) of this section shall render any such person liable to any punishment if he/she proves that the offence was committed without his/her knowledge, consent or connivance, and that he/she had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 124. General Penalties Where no specific penalty is prescribed in this Law or in any
chunks.text: 124. General Penalties Where no specific penalty is prescribed in this Law or in any regulations made pursuant to this Law for any offence, a person found guilty of such offence shall: (a) as a first offender, be liable to a fine not less than Five Hundred Thousand Naira (N500,000.00) for an individual or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one (1) year, or to both such fine and 71 imprisonment and in the case of a body corporate, it shall be l iable to a fine of not less than Two Million Naira (N2,000,0000.00); and (b) for a subsequent conviction, to a fine not less than One Million Naira (N1,000,0000.00) for an individual or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three (3) years or to both such fine and imprisonment and in the case of a body corporate, it shall be liable to a fine not less than Five Million Naira (N5,000,000.00).

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 125. Whistle Blowing Provisions (1) Any person shall have the right to report or disc
chunks.text: 125. Whistle Blowing Provisions (1) Any person shall have the right to report or disclose in good faith and in the public interest either orally or in writing, any suspected violations of any provis ion of this Law or applicable regulations to the Commission. A disclosure is made in good faith if it is made honestly and with due care. (2) A qualifying disclosure shall be construed to mean any disclosure, made in good faith and in the public interest, of information regarding any conduct by which the whistleblower has reason to believe and tends to show any of the following: (a) that an offence under this Law or applicable regulations has occurred or is likely to occur; (b) that a person has failed, is failin g or is likely to fail to comply with any legal obligation provided under this Law or applicable regulations; (c) that a person is carrying on activities relating to electricity that may constitute a risk to health or safety of the general public; or (d) that there is damage to electricity property or concealment of the same. (3) Upon receipt of a report by the Commission, the Commission shall take all necessary steps to investigate the report and if satisfied that any offence under this Law has been committed or there was an attempt to commit an offence under this Law , the Commission shall liaise with the Power Enforcement Unit for the prosecution of the offender. (4) The Commission shall always keep confidential all disclosed information so that it is not exposed to, or used by unauthorized persons. (5) The Commission shall give every and all necessary protection to the life, character and fundamental rights of any whistleblower for the purpose of this section. (6) The Commission shall by regulations set up a n incentive scheme for the provision of monetary reward of a minimum amount of One Hundred Thousand Naira (N100,000.00) or such larger amount as may be fixed by the Commission , which shall be given to any person who makes a report or disclosure in accordance with subsection (1) of this section and the Commission is able to establish that an offence has been committed or there was an attempt to commit an offence as a result of such report or disclosu

chunks.text: 126. Criminal Jurisdiction The Special Offences Court or any other court shall have jurisdiction to try any person for any offence specified in this Law or any applicable regulations. 72 PART XIX TRANSITION TO THE PLATEAU STATE ELECTRICITY MARKET

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 128. Alternative Dispute Resolution Framework The Commission shall take steps to faci
chunks.text: 128. Alternative Dispute Resolution Framework The Commission shall take steps to facilitate the amicable and expeditious resolution of disputes in the Plateau State Electricity Market, including through c ollaboration with the Plateau State Multi Door Court House.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 129. Procedure for Cause of Action (1) A suit against the Commission or the Agency or
chunks.text: 129. Procedure for Cause of Action (1) A suit against the Commission or the Agency or any member, officer or employee of the Commission or the Agency for any act done, attempted to be done or omitted to be done in pursuance or execution of this Law, any other Laws, applicable regulations, or of any public duty or authority shall not lie or be instituted in any court unless it is commenced within twelve (12) months after the act, neglect or default complained of or in case of continuance of damage or injury within twelve (12) months after. (2) A suit shall not be commenced against the Commission or the Agency or any board member, officer or employee of the Commission or the Agency before the expiration of a p eriod of thirty (30) days after written notice of intention to commence the suit shall have been served upon the Commission or the Agency by the intending Claimant or Claimant’s agent. (3) The notice referred to in subsection (1) of this section shall clearly and explicitly state: (a) the cause of action; 74 (b) the particulars of the claim; (c) the name and place of abode of the intending Claimant; and (d) the reliefs which are claimed. (4) The Notice referred to in subsection (1) of this section and any summons or other documents required or authorized to be served on the Commission or the Agency, may be served by delivering the same to the office of the Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer or Secretary of the Commission or the office of the Chairperson, Managing Director or Secretary of the Agency.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 130. Exemption from Liability No liability shall attach to the Commission or the Agen
chunks.text: 130. Exemption from Liability No liability shall attach to the Commission or the Agency or any member, officer or employee of the Commission or the Agency for any loss or damage sustained by any person done in good faith in exercise or performance of any function conferred or imposed on the Commission or the Agency or any of the member, officer or employee of the Commission or the Agency pursuant to this Law.

chunks.title: PART XX – GENERAL PROVISIONS — 131. Transitional Provisions Applicable to the Agency (1) All existing electrical ins
chunks.text: 131. Transitional Provisions Applicable to the Agency (1) All existing electrical installations which were the property of the State or the Plateau State Electricity Board immediately before the enactment of the Law and any future electrical installations and assets owned by the State, shall by virtue of this Law vest in the Agency. (2) All undischarged liabilities and obligations of the State or the Plateau State Electricity Board in respect of any transferred electrical installation, shall from the commencement date of this Law become the liabilities and obligations of the Agency. (3) Every contract, instrument or arrangement in which the State or the Plateau State Electricity Board was a party to for the construction of any transferred electrical installation shall, unless the circumstances otherwise require, have the effect from the commencement date of this Law as if the Agency had been a party to it an d any reference to the State or the Plateau State Electricity Board in the contract or instrument shall be deemed to be a reference to the Agency. (4) From the commencement date of this Law, employees of the Plateau State Electricity Board shall be employees of the Agency on terms no less favourable to those in effect immediately prior to the transfer, and all years of service with the Plateau State Electricity Board shall be deemed to be years of service with the Agency. 132. Repeal The Plateau State Electric Power Sector Reform Law 2018 is hereby repealed.
